G-265Batch learningTraining on the whole dataset at once, offline, then deploying.Note ML-004Batch (offline) learning
G-266Batch normalisationA layer placed between layers of a network that re-centres and re-scales its inputs during training; this keeps the activations away from the flat ends of sigmoid and tanh, which helps against vanishing gradients.Note DL-018Batch normalisation
G-267Batch sizeThe number of rows in each batch; a hyperparameter.Note ML-059Mini-batch gradient descent
G-2215Bayes factorA number that says how strongly the evidence favours yes over no: how many times more likely the evidence is if the answer is yes than if it is no, P(evidence∣yes)/P(evidence∣no). Multiplying the prior odds by it gives the posterior odds.Note MA-019Bayes’ theorem
G-269Bayes’ theoremThe rule that reverses a conditional probability: from P(B∣A) it gives P(A∣B), so a belief about A can be updated after seeing B; P(A∣B)=P(B∣A)P(A)/P(B).Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-270Bayesian optimisationTuning that builds a model of how the score depends on the settings (hyperparameters) and uses all earlier trials to choose the next one.Note ML-128Bayesian optimisation
G-271Bayesian statisticsThe branch of statistics that treats probabilities as beliefs updated by Bayes’ theorem.Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-272Beam searchA way of producing the output sentence (a decoding method) that keeps several candidate sentences at each step and picks the most probable complete one.Note DL-085Transformer inference (autoregressive decoding, KV cache, beam search)
G-273BeautifulSoupPython library that parses HTML into a searchable tree.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-274Bell curveThe curve of a normal distribution.Note ML-041Normal distribution
G-275Bernoulli distributionThe distribution of a single trial with two outcomes, such as one coin toss: 1 (success) with probability p, 0 (failure) with probability 1−p.Note MA-021Bernoulli and binomial distributions
G-276Bernoulli trialOne random experiment with exactly two outcomes, success (1) and failure (0).Note MA-031Bernoulli and binomial distributions
G-277BernoulliNBNaive Bayes for binary (yes/no) inputs.Note ML-084Naive Bayes
G-278BERTA published transformer trained on a large amount of English text; BERT-base has 12 layers of 12 heads.Note DL-078Transformer
G-279Bessel’s correctionDividing by n−1 instead of n, so the sample variance is right on average.Note MA-006Bessel’s correction
G-280Best-fit lineThe line with the smallest total error over all the training points.Note ML-049Best-fit line and squared error
G-281best_score_The best mean cross-validated score found by a search.Note ML-028Hyperparameter tuning
G-282Beta testingReleasing a new version to a small group of trusted users first.Note ML-009Beta and A/B testing
G-283BFGSThe most used way to take Newton-like steps without computing second derivatives (a quasi-Newton method): it builds a stand-in for the Hessian from gradients alone, kept symmetric and positive definite.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-287Bias (of a model)Error from a model being too simple to capture the true relationship.Note ML-061Bias-variance trade-off
G-284Bias (of a perceptron)The weight on a constant input of 1; it shifts the boundary away from the origin.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-285Bias correctionA fix for a running average (EWMA) that starts at 0 and is too small in the first steps: divide it by 1−βt.Note DL-038Adam
G-286Bias vector (bk)A column holding one bias per node of layer k; it is added to the layer’s weighted sums before the activation.Note DL-010Forward propagation
G-288Bias-variance trade-offLowering bias by adding complexity tends to raise variance, and the reverse.Note ML-061Bias-variance trade-off
G-289Biased estimatorA formula for estimating a value from data (an estimator) that is systematically too high or too low on average.Note MA-071Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-290Biased modelA model pushed towards wrong answers, e.g. by bad data.Note ML-005Online learning
G-291Bidirectional encoderAn encoder with one RNN reading forwards and one backwards, whose states are joined at each position.Note DL-066Bidirectional RNNs
G-292Bidirectional RNNTwo RNNs reading a sequence in opposite directions, their hidden states joined at every time step, so the output at each word uses the words both before and after it.Note DL-066Bidirectional RNNs
G-293Big modelThe paper’s larger transformer: dmodel​=1024, dff​=4096, 16 heads, 213 million parameters.Note DL-086The transformer end to end (capstone)
G-294Big pictureThe end product and how it will be used, which decides the type of ML problem.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-2269BigramA pair of consecutive words; the bigram rule guesses the word that most often follows the previous one.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-295BiLSTM, BiGRUA bidirectional RNN made of LSTM or GRU layers.Note DL-066Bidirectional RNNs
G-296BimodalA distribution with two peaks.Note ML-030Kurtosis and moments
G-298BinOne of the equal ranges a histogram splits the data into.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-297Bin edgeA boundary between two neighbouring bins.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-299bin_edges_The fitted KBinsDiscretizer attribute holding the learned edges.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-300BinarizationTurning a continuous column into 0 or 1 by comparing it with one threshold.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-301Binarizerscikit-learn’s class for binarization, with parameters threshold and copy.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-302Binary classifierA model that separates exactly two classes.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-303Binary cross entropy (log loss)The loss function of logistic regression for two classes: per row −yloga−(1−y)log(1−a), averaged over the rows (the average cross entropy).Note ML-072Log loss (binary cross entropy)
G-305Binary fileA file that is not plain text, such as a saved model.Note ML-009Deployment
G-306Binary image classificationSorting photos into one of two classes, such as cat or dog.Note DL-049Image classification with a CNN (cats vs dogs)
G-307BinningGrouping a numerical column into ranges that act as categories.Note ML-022Binning and binarization
G-308Binomial distributionThe distribution of the number of successes in n independent trials with the same success probability.Note MA-031Bernoulli and binomial distributions
G-309Binomial experimentA fixed number n of independent Bernoulli trials with the same success probability p.Note MA-031Bernoulli and binomial distributions
G-2246Binomial test (exact test)A test of a proportion that adds up binomial probabilities of every count as rare as the observed one or rarer.Note MA-044One-sample proportion test
G-310Bivariate analysisStudying two columns together to see how they are related, for example with a scatter plot or a bar plot.Note ML-019Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-311Black box model (black box)A model whose inner workings are hidden: it gives predictions without showing how each input contributed.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-313Blank mapA feature map that is entirely zero for a given photo: its pattern is nowhere in the photo.Note DL-052Visualising what a CNN learns
G-314BlendingA form of stacking in which the final model (the meta-model) is trained on the base models’ predictions for a hold-out validation set.Note ML-121Stacking and blending
G-315BLEU scoreA measure of translation quality: how many word sequences of a translation match a human reference.Note DL-067Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-316BMIBody mass index: weight (kg) divided by height (m) squared.Note ML-007Poor-quality data
G-317Boolean indexingSelecting rows with an array of True/False values, e.g. X[y_means == 0].Note ML-123K-means
G-318BoostingCombining many simple models one after another to reduce bias, the error of a model that is too simple.Note ML-095Boosting
G-320bootstrapBaggingClassifier setting: draw rows with replacement (True, bagging) or without (False, pasting).Note ML-100Bagging
G-319Bootstrap sampleA sample of the same size as the data, drawn with replacement so some rows repeat and others are left out; each tree of a random forest gets its own, so the trees differ.Note ML-102Random forest
G-321bootstrap_featuresBaggingClassifier setting: draw columns with replacement or without.Note ML-100Bagging
G-322BootstrappingDrawing random samples of the data to train each base model.Note ML-095Bagging
G-323Border pointIn DBSCAN, a point with fewer than MinPts points within eps but with a core point among them; it sits on the edge of a cluster and joins its nearest core point’s cluster.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-324Boston housing data506 Boston districts, 13 inputs and the median home value; removed from scikit-learn in version 1.2.Note ML-093Regression trees
G-325BotA program that visits websites automatically.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-326BottleneckA single fixed-size vector through which all information about the input must pass; in the plain encoder–decoder it is the context vector, and a long sentence does not fit in it.Note DL-069Attention mechanism
G-327Bounded functionA function whose values stay within a fixed range, such as −1 to 1 for sine.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-328Bounding boxA rectangle drawn around an object to show where it is in a photo.Note DL-051Pretrained models and ImageNet
G-329Box plotA graph of a column’s five-number summary, a box with whiskers and outliers drawn as dots; it shows the centre, spread and outliers at a glance.Note ML-019Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-330Box-and-whisker plotAnother name for a box plot: the graph of a column’s five-number summary, drawn as a box with whiskers and outliers as dots.Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-331Box-Cox transformA power transform that reshapes a feature of positive values to look closer to normal, with a parameter λ fitted to the data: (xλ−1)/λ, or lnx when λ=0.Note ML-030Power transformer
G-332Branch (subtree)A node together with everything below it.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-333BroadcastingNumPy stretching a single number (a scalar) or a smaller array to match a bigger array before an operation.Note MA-049Vector magnitude, distance and scalar operations
G-334Buying behaviourThe pattern of what a customer buys.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-335Byte pair encoding (BPE)A way to build a tokenizer’s vocabulary: start from single bytes and repeatedly merge the most frequent pair of symbols into a new token, so any text can be cut into tokens from a fixed vocabulary.Note DL-087Tokenization and integer encoding of text
G-337C (LogisticRegression)The setting that controls how strongly LogisticRegression is regularised: C is the inverse of the regularisation strength, so smaller C means stronger regularisation.Note ML-080Regularisation
G-336C (SVM)The weight on the classification error; a large C means few mistakes and a narrow margin, a small C a wide margin.Note ML-088Support vector machines
G-338Cache memoryA small, fast memory inside the processor that holds data used again and again.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-339CalculusThe branch of mathematics about change: differentiation and integration.Note MA-001Role of mathematics in ML
G-340CalibratedClassifierCVscikit-learn wrapper that makes a classifier with no probabilities by default, such as an SVM, give calibrated probabilities.Note ML-097Voting ensembles
G-2223California housing data20,640 California districts (1990), 8 features and the median house value; built into scikit-learn.Note ML-093Regression trees
G-341CallbackAn object whose code Keras runs at set points during training, for example after every epoch.Note DL-022Early stopping
G-342Candidate cell state (c~t​)In an LSTM, the new values that could be added to the long-term memory (cell state), made by a tanh layer.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-343Candidate hidden state (h~t​)The proposed new memory, built by a tanh layer from the reset memory and the input.Note DL-064GRU (gated recurrent unit)
G-344CapacityA model’s ability to fit a wide variety of functions; too much capacity for the data leads to overfitting.Note DL-026Overfitting
G-345CappingReplacing every value beyond a limit with the limit itself.Note ML-040Capping (winsorization)
G-346cars.csvdtreeviz’s sample data: 392 cars with MPG, weight, engine size and cylinders.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-347CARTClassification and regression trees: the tree algorithm used for both kinds of problem.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-348CatBoostYandex’s gradient boosting library, with built-in handling of categorical columns.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-349Categorical cross entropyThe loss for classification with more than two classes and a softmax output: the average of minus the log of the probability given to the true class, −∑j​yj​logy^​j​ per row with one-hot labels; it is small when the true class gets a high probability.Note ML-078Categorical and sparse categorical cross-entropy
G-351Categorical data (categorical column)Data made of categories: labels rather than numbers.Note ML-003Encoding categorical data
G-352Categorical distributionThe distribution of one trial with more than two outcomes; Bernoulli is its two-outcome case.Note MA-031Bernoulli and binomial distributions
G-353CategoricalNBscikit-learn’s Naive Bayes for categorical inputs.Note ML-083Naive Bayes
G-354categories_The attribute holding the categories OrdinalEncoder learned, in order.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-356CategoryOne of the fixed groups of a categorical column.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-355Category shareThe rows in one category divided by the rows that have a value.Note ML-036Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
G-357Causal (look-ahead) maskThe mask with −∞ above the diagonal, so every word attends only to itself and the words before it; used in training and at inference.Note DL-082Masked self-attention
G-359CausationA cause-and-effect relationship: changing one thing changes the other.Note MA-009Correlation and causation
G-360ccp_alphaThe penalty per leaf used to cut a fully grown tree back (cost-complexity pruning strength).Note ML-105Decision trees
G-362CellOne block of a notebook, holding either code or Markdown.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-361Cell state (ct​)The LSTM’s long-term memory: a vector passed from step to step beside the hidden state; the gates add to it and remove from it, so information can be kept over many steps.Note DL-061LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-363Central differenceA way to estimate a slope from two nearby points, one small step h on each side: (f(x+h)−f(x−h))/(2h) (a numerical derivative). It is more accurate than a one-sided step.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-364Central limit theoremFor large enough samples, the means of many samples follow a normal distribution centred on the population mean, whatever the shape of the data (if its variance is finite); this justifies confidence intervals and hypothesis tests on means.Note MA-033Central limit theorem
G-365Centred dataData whose mean is 0, made by subtracting the mean from every value; some algorithms need it.Note ML-024Normalization
G-367CentroidThe centre point of one cluster in k-means, the mean of the points in it; every point is assigned to its nearest centroid.Note ML-122K-means
G-366Centroid initializationPicking the first k centroids, here at random from the data.Note ML-122K-means
G-368Centroid-based clusteringClustering in which each group has a centre point (a centroid) and every point belongs to the group whose centre is nearest, as in k-means.Note ML-126K-means
G-371Chain ruleTo differentiate a function of a function, multiply the outer derivative by the inner derivative.Note ML-073Derivatives of one variable
G-369Chain rule of probabilityWriting a joint probability as a product of conditional probabilities, one variable at a time.Note ML-082Naive Bayes
G-370Chain rule with JacobiansThe chain rule for functions with many inputs and outputs: the table of derivatives (Jacobian) of one function applied after another is the product of their two Jacobians, in the same order.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-372Chained assignmentSelecting part of a DataFrame and then changing that selection in a second step; does nothing in pandas 3.Note ML-044Feature construction and splitting
G-373Chained equationsA way to fill gaps in several columns at once: each column gets its own prediction model, which fills its gaps using the latest fills of the other columns (the method behind MICE).Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-2272Change ΔeThe amount attention adds to a word’s vector: the attention output is added to the word’s own vector (the residual connection), new vector =e+Δe, so it acts as an update to the word.Note DL-076Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-374Change of basis matrixA matrix P that translates between two sets of axes: its columns are the new axes (basis vectors). P−1AP is the same transformation as A seen in the new axes; in an eigenbasis it only scales.Note MA-056Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-375ChannelOne colour layer of an image (red, green or blue).Note ML-010Tensors
G-376Characteristic polynomialA polynomial built from a square matrix A, det(A−λI), whose roots are the eigenvalues of A, so solving it finds them.Note MA-056Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-377Checkpoint averagingAveraging the weights of the last few saved copies of a model.Note DL-086Learning-rate warm-up schedule
G-378Chi-square distributionThe shape the chi-square statistic χ2 follows when the null hypothesis H0​ is true: never negative, skewed to the right, with one parameter, the degrees of freedom.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-379Chi-square statistic χ2A number that measures the total mismatch between observed and expected counts, ∑(O−E)2/E; it is 0 when every count matches and grows as they differ.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-381Chi-square testA test of whether categorical counts match expected counts (goodness of fit) or whether two categorical columns are related (independence).Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-380Chi-square test of independenceA chi-square test of whether two categorical columns are related; df=(r−1)(c−1).Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-382Chi-squared test (chi2)A test scoring how strongly a column is linked to the target; needs values of 0 or more.Note ML-028Feature selection
G-383Cholesky solverA scikit-learn Ridge solver that computes the coefficients in one go from the formula (the closed-form solution) instead of by repeated steps.Note ML-063Ridge regression
G-384ChordThe straight line joining two points on a function’s graph; it is used to test convexity: a convex function never rises above any of its chords.Note MA-065Convex and non-convex loss
G-385ChunkA piece of a file read as a small DataFrame, so a file too large for memory can be processed one piece at a time.Note ML-014CSV files
G-387ChurnCustomers leaving a platform or service.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-386Churn rateThe percentage of customers who leave during a given period.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-389Class (HTML)An attribute that labels tags; used to select the right ones.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-388Class priorThe share of training rows in a class, such as 5 wins out of 8 matches; Naive Bayes uses it as the prior probability of that class.Note ML-081Naive Bayes
G-390class_sepmake_classification setting for how far apart the classes are.Note ML-070Perceptron trick
G-391class_weightA setting that weights each class’s mistakes in the loss; “balanced” helps rare classes.Note ML-080Imbalanced data
G-392classes_The attribute holding the classes LabelEncoder learned, in order.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-395ClassificationPredicting which of a fixed set of categories (classes) a row belongs to, learned from examples whose answers are known (supervised learning with a categorical output).Note ML-003Classification problems
G-393Classification error (SVM)The part of the soft-margin SVM loss that adds up every point’s slack ξi​ (how far the point sits on the wrong side of its own hyperplane): ∑ξi​, the total slack of all points.Note ML-088Hinge loss and soft margin
G-394Classification metricA number that measures how well a classification model performs.Note ML-075Accuracy
G-396classification_reportscikit-learn function that prints precision, recall, F1 and support for every class.Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-397Client, serverThe program that asks, and the computer that answers.Note ML-016APIs
G-398Closed-form solutionAn answer given directly by a formula of ordinary operations.Note ML-050Ordinary least squares (closed form)
G-399ClusterOne group found by clustering.Note ML-003Clustering
G-400cluster_centers_The coordinates of the final centroids of a fitted KMeans.Note ML-123K-means
G-401ClusteringSplitting data into groups of similar rows.Note ML-003Clustering
G-402ClustermapA heatmap with rows and columns reordered so similar ones sit together.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-403CNN architectureThe sequence of layers of a CNN: convolution and pooling blocks, Flatten, fully connected layers, output.Note DL-045CNN architecture (LeNet-5)
G-404Co-occurrence probabilityHow likely word k is to appear near word i in the training text, written Pik​; GloVe trains word vectors from these probabilities.Note DL-072Meaning as direction in embedding space
G-405CodomainThe set in which a function’s outputs lie.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-406coef_The fitted slope (one per input column) in scikit-learn.Note ML-049Simple linear regression
G-407Coefficient (βi​)The weight of one input column: the change in the output per unit of that input, others fixed.Note ML-052Multiple linear regression
G-408Coefficient of variation (CV)Standard deviation divided by mean: spread relative to the average.Note MA-006Variance
G-409Coefficient pathHow each coefficient changes as the regularisation strength grows, drawn as one line per feature, so we can see which coefficients are shrunk towards 0.Note ML-065Ridge regression
G-410Coefficient vector (β)All the coefficients of the model, β0​ to βm​, as one column.Note ML-053Multiple linear regression
G-411Colour blobA filter that responds to one colour.Note DL-052Visualising what a CNN learns
G-412Column blockXGBoost’s storage of the data one sorted column per block, so each core can work on one feature.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-413Column sampling (feature sampling)Training each model of an ensemble (each base model) on a random subset of the columns.Note ML-102Random forest
G-414Column spaceEvery output a matrix can produce: all the vectors made by scaling and adding its columns (the span of its columns).Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-415Column transformerA scikit-learn class that applies different transformations to different columns at once and joins the results.Note ML-027Column transformer
G-416Column vectorA vector written as one column, shape n×1; the default meaning of “vector”.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-417ColumnTransformerThe scikit-learn class (in sklearn.compose) that implements the column transformer.Note ML-027Column transformer
G-418Combined samplingTraining each model of an ensemble (each base model) on random rows and random columns together.Note ML-102Random forest
G-419Combining perceptronsFeeding several perceptrons’ outputs, weighted and with a bias, into another perceptron, so their straight boundaries combine into a curved decision boundary; this is a multi-layer perceptron.Note DL-009Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-420Commutative lawThe rule that swapping the two vectors does not change their dot product: a⋅b=b⋅a.Note MA-050Dot product
G-421CompileChoosing the loss, the optimizer and the metrics before training.Note DL-011Keras workflow
G-422Complement (Ac)The event that A does not happen: every outcome not in A.Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-423Complement ruleThe probability that an event does not happen is 1 minus the probability that it does, P(Ac)=1−P(A); useful when the opposite event is easier to count, as in at least one head.Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-424Complementary slacknessA rule the best answer must obey when there are inequality constraints: for each constraint, its multiplier or the constraint value is 0, λi​gi​(x)=0, so a constraint that plays no part at the answer gets multiplier 0. It is one of the KKT conditions.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-426Complete caseA row with a value in every column used.Note ML-034Complete case analysis
G-425Complete case analysis (CCA)Dropping every row that has a missing value in any chosen column; also called listwise deletion.Note ML-034Complete case analysis
G-427Complete linkageA way to measure the distance between two clusters in hierarchical clustering: the distance of their farthest pair of points; the closest two clusters are merged next.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-428Complex cellA nerve cell in the brain’s first visual area (V1) that responds to its preferred edge anywhere inside a larger patch of view (receptive field).Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-429ComponentOne number of a vector, its position along one axis.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-430components_The directions of the principal components found by a fitted PCA (the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix), one per row.Note ML-048PCA
G-431CompositionApplying one transformation and then another, seen as one overall transformation.Note MA-054Matrix multiplication as composition
G-432Compound eventAn event with two or more outcomes.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-433CompressionStoring data in fewer bits, for example by throwing away detail the eye barely notices and not storing again what stays the same between video frames, so files take less space and are faster to send.Note ML-010Tensors
G-434Computation graphA function broken into elementary steps, each a node, with arrows for the flow of values. Backpropagation walks it backwards, applying the chain rule one step at a time.Note MA-063Backpropagation
G-435Concat scoreA score for how useful an encoder state is now: join the decoder state and the encoder state into one vector and pass it through a tanh layer and one output unit to get one number, va⊤​tanh(Wa​[si​;hj​]). It is Luong’s name for the additive (Bahdanau) attention score.Note DL-070Bahdanau (additive) attention
G-436Concatenation ([ht−1​,xt​])Joining two vectors end to end into one longer vector, so one layer can read both at once: 3 numbers and 4 numbers give 7.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-438Concave functionA function shaped like an upside-down bowl, the negative of a convex function: every chord lies on or below its graph, as for lnx. Maximising a concave function is the same task as minimising a convex one.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-2256Concave up, concave downCalculus names for a cup-shaped (convex) and a hump-shaped (concave) part of a curve.Note MA-067Convex and non-convex loss
G-2165ConceptOne idea on the Course map, such as overfitting or Ridge. Links join Concepts, and each Concept points to the Note that teaches it.Course map
G-2162Concept mapThe view of the Course map that joins Concepts by typed Links (needs, is a kind of, fixes, compared with, used in), so we can see what each idea depends on and what it is for.Course map
G-439condaA package and environment manager: it installs Python and libraries and keeps each set in a separate environment, so different projects do not clash.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-440conda-forgeA free, community-run channel (an online store of conda packages) with more packages, often newer ones, than Anaconda’s default channel.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-441Condition numberA number that says how much a matrix can magnify small errors, such as rounding errors, when we solve with it; a large value means the answer is sensitive. It is the largest singular value over the smallest, σ1​/σn​.Note MA-058Singular value decomposition
G-442Conditional hyperparameterA hyperparameter that exists only for some values of another, such as units_3.Note DL-039Keras Tuner
G-443Conditional independenceIndependence that holds once a third variable is known: given the class, knowing one feature tells nothing more about another. Naive Bayes assumes it so it can multiply one probability per feature.Note ML-082Naive Bayes
G-444Conditional probabilityThe probability of an event given that another event has happened: P(A∣B).Note MA-015Conditional probability
G-445Condorcet’s jury theoremA majority of independent voters, each right with probability above 0.5, is right more often than any one voter, and more so as voters are added.Note ML-096Voting ensembles
G-446Confidence intervalA range of values, computed from a sample, that we expect to contain a population parameter such as the mean, so it shows how uncertain the estimate is. The method captures the true value in a stated share of repeated samples, such as 95%.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-447Confidence levelThe share of intervals built by the method that contain the parameter, such as 95%; written 1−α.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-448Confounding variableA hidden factor that drives two variables and makes them correlated.Note MA-009Correlation and causation
G-449Confusion matrixA table counting a classifier’s predictions for every pair of actual and predicted class, so we can see which kinds of mistake it makes, which accuracy alone hides.Note ML-075Confusion matrix
G-450Connection objectThe open link to a database (conn) that queries go through.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-451ConnectorA library that lets Python talk to a database.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-2238Conservative degrees of freedomThe hand-calculation shortcut min(n1​,n2​)−1 for a two-sample t-test; Welch’s formula is closer to exact.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-452Consistency (of an estimator)Getting closer to the true parameter value as the amount of data grows.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-453Constituency parsingFinding the grammatical tree of a sentence: its phrases and how they nest.Note DL-086The transformer end to end (capstone)
G-454Constrained formWriting regularisation as: make the loss as small as possible while the coefficients stay inside a fixed budget (a circle for Ridge). The picture shows how the penalty limits the size of the coefficients.Note ML-065Ridge regression
G-455Constrained optimisationMaximising or minimising a function while keeping one or more constraints true.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-456ConstraintA condition the solution must satisfy; in SVM, yi​(wTxi​+b)≥1 for every training point.Note ML-087Support vector machines
G-457Constructor (__init__)The method that runs when an object is created and stores its settings.Note ML-124K-means
G-458ContainerA tag (often a div) that holds everything about one item, such as one company.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-459Context sizeThe largest number of tokens the model can read at once: 1,024 for GPT-2, 2,048 for GPT-3.Note DL-087Decoder-only GPT
G-461Context vectorThe summary of the input that the decoder works from; one fixed vector in the plain encoder–decoder, a new one per output word with attention.Note DL-067Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-460Context vector ci​The summary of the input made fresh for each decoder step i under attention: a weighted sum of all the encoder’s hidden states, where the weights decide how much each input word counts for the word being written now.Note DL-069Attention mechanism
G-462Contextual embeddingA vector for a word that changes with the other words of its sentence, so “bank” gets one vector in “river bank” and another in “money bank”. Self-attention produces it.Note DL-073Contextual embeddings
G-463Contextual learningStudying a maths topic together with the ML algorithm that uses it, instead of the whole subject up front.Note MA-002How to learn the maths for ML
G-464Contingency tableA table that counts the observations for every pair of categories of two categorical features, so we can see whether the two are related; also called a crosstab.Note MA-013Venn diagrams and contingency tables
G-465Continuous dataNumerical data that can take any value in a range.Note MA-004Discrete and continuous data
G-466Continuous random variableA random variable that can take any value in a range, such as a CGPA.Note MA-020Random variables
G-467Continuous uniform distribution U(a,b)A continuous variable spread evenly between a and b, with density 1/(b−a).Note MA-029Uniform distribution
G-468Contour plotA map of a surface seen from above, with lines joining points of equal height, so a 3D shape such as a loss bowl can be drawn and read on flat paper.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-469ConvergeTo settle at a minimum, with steps becoming negligible.Note DL-017Gradient descent
G-470Convergence (k-means)The point where the centroids stop moving between rounds, so the algorithm stops.Note ML-122K-means
G-472Convergence (MICE)The point where the fills hardly change between two iterations.Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-471Convergence speedHow many epochs a method needs to reach a good solution, as opposed to the time per epoch.Note DL-020Gradient descent
G-473ConvergenceWarningA warning that the solver stopped at max_iter before reaching the minimum.Note ML-080Logistic regression
G-474Conversion rateThe share of people reached who become customers.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-475Convex combinationA mix of points (or functions) using non-negative shares that add up to 1, such as 30% of one and 70% of another; for two points it gives a point on the segment between them.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-476Convex functionA function where a straight line between any two points of its curve never goes below the curve; it has a single minimum.Note ML-056Convex and non-convex loss
G-477Convex hullThe smallest region with straight edges that contains a set of points; every weighted average of the points lies inside it.Note DL-076Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-478Convex optimisation problemA search for the lowest point of a bowl-shaped (convex) function inside an allowed region with no dents or holes (convex inequality constraints, affine equality constraints). In such a problem every local minimum is the global one.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-479Convex setA set that contains the whole segment between any two of its points.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-480Convolution layerA layer that slides small filters over its input to find features.Note DL-040Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-481Convolution operationSliding a small filter over an input and, at each position, multiplying cell by cell and adding up, so the output (a feature map) is large where the input contains the filter’s pattern, such as an edge.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-482Convolutional baseThe convolution and pooling layers of a CNN, which find features in the image.Note DL-053Transfer learning (feature extraction and fine-tuning)
G-484Convolutional neural network (CNN)A neural network that slides small filters over its input to find patterns such as edges, using at least one convolutional layer; the standard network for images.Note DL-040Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-485Coordinate descentAn optimisation method that updates one coefficient at a time; used by scikit-learn’s Lasso.Note ML-067Lasso regression
G-2241Coordinates (of a vector)The numbers of a vector, read as walking instructions from the origin to its tip: the first says how far to walk along the x-axis, the second how far to walk up or down.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-486Core pointIn DBSCAN, a point with at least MinPts points within distance eps of it; core points form the inside of a cluster and give it its shape.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-487Corrected resampled t-testA paired t-test for comparing two models’ cross-validation scores that enlarges the variance to allow for the folds sharing most of their training data, so it does not report a “significant” difference too often.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-490CorrelationA number from -1 to +1 that says how strongly two numerical features rise or fall together along a straight line: the covariance divided by both standard deviations, so the units drop out.Note MA-009Correlation
G-488Correlation between base modelsHow alike two base models’ predictions are; the less alike, the more an ensemble cuts variance.Note ML-104Random forest
G-489Correlation testA t-test of whether a sample correlation r is strong enough to show that two numerical features are correlated in the population (H0​:ρ=0). It uses t=rn−2​/1−r2​ with n−2 degrees of freedom.Note MA-044Correlation significance test
G-491Cosine similarityA score from -1 to 1 for how closely two vectors point the same way: the cosine of the angle between them. It ignores their lengths, so it compares texts or word embeddings by direction only.Note MA-050Cosine similarity
G-492Cost functionA measure of how far a model’s predictions are from the true values, averaged over the data and read as a function of the model’s parameters; training looks for the parameters that make it smallest. Often another name for the loss function.Note MA-065Convex and non-convex loss
G-2222Cost-complexity pruningGrowing a tree fully, then cutting back the leaves that buy the least fit: keep the subtree with the lowest leaf impurity + α × number of leaves.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-493Cost-sensitive learningChanging the learning so that mistakes on some classes cost more.Note ML-127Cost-sensitive learning
G-494Count plotA bar chart with one bar per category, as tall as its frequency.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-2160Course mapThe overview that ties all Notes together in four views (Pipeline map, Concept map, Learning path, Algorithm chooser): where each idea sits in a project, how ideas connect, what to read first and which algorithm to choose.Course map
G-496CovarianceA number that says how two numerical features move together: positive if they rise together, negative if one rises as the other falls. Its size depends on the units.Note MA-009Covariance and covariance matrix
G-495Covariance matrixA square table with every feature’s variance on the diagonal and every pair’s covariance off it, so it sums up how the data spreads and which features move together; PCA takes its eigenvectors.Note ML-047Covariance and covariance matrix
G-497Covariate shiftA change in the distribution of a model’s inputs while the input-output relationship stays the same.Note DL-031Covariate shift
G-498CoverXGBoost’s measure of how much data a node holds, as its similarity score counts it: the sum of p(1−p) over the node’s observations in classification, the number of observations in regression. The tree dump prints it as cover.Note ML-119XGBoost
G-499CoverageThe share of intervals from repeated samples that contain the true parameter; equals the confidence level when the assumptions hold.Note MA-036Confidence intervals
G-500Cramér’s VA measure of how strongly two categorical features are related, from 0 (no relationship) to 1 (perfect relationship), made by rescaling the chi-square statistic.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-501Credible intervalThe Bayesian counterpart of a confidence interval: a range that, after seeing the data, holds the parameter with a stated probability such as 0.95. So it can be read as “95% probability the parameter is in here”, which a confidence interval cannot.Note MA-036Confidence intervals
G-502Credit scoringPredicting whether a loan applicant will repay.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-503criterionThe DecisionTreeClassifier hyperparameter choosing the impurity measure: “gini” (default), “entropy” or “log_loss”.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-504Critical valueThe cut-off on a z (or t) curve that leaves α/2 in each tail; a confidence interval reaches this many standard errors either side of the estimate. It is 1.96 for 95% on the standard normal curve.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-505Cross entropyA loss for classifiers that grows when the model gives a low probability to the true class. It is the negative log-likelihood, so minimising it maximises the likelihood; smaller is better.Note ML-072Log loss (binary cross entropy)
G-506Cross product (vector product)A product of two 3D vectors that gives a vector perpendicular to both.Note MA-050Dot product
G-507Cross-attentionAttention between the two halves of a transformer: the queries come from the decoder and the keys and values from the encoder’s output, so each output word can use the input sentence.Note DL-083Cross-attention
G-508Cross-correlationThe slide, multiply and add of a CNN filter done without first flipping the filter; a true convolution flips it. Most deep learning libraries compute cross-correlation and call it convolution, which does not matter because the filter values are learned.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-509Cross-validated accuracyAccuracy averaged over several train-test splits of the data, an estimate of performance on new data.Note ML-031Cross-validation
G-510Cross-validationTesting a model by training and testing it several times on different parts of the training data.Note ML-028Cross-validation
G-511CrosstabA table that counts the rows for every pair of categories of two categorical columns, so we can see whether the two are related; pandas builds it with pd.crosstab. Also called a contingency table.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-512CrowdsourcingSplitting a large task, such as labelling, among many paid online workers.Note DL-051Pretrained models and ImageNet
G-513CSV fileA text file holding a table, with commas between values.Note ML-014CSV files
G-514CUDANVIDIA’s platform for programming GPUs, so a network’s matrix multiplications can run in parallel on a GPU; it made training on GPUs practical.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-515Cumulative distribution function (CDF)For every value x, the probability that the random variable comes out at most x: P(X≤x).Note MA-021Cumulative distribution function (CDF)
G-516Cumulative explained varianceThe share of the data’s variance kept by the first k principal components together; its curve over k is used to choose how many components to keep.Note ML-048PCA
G-517Cumulative frequencyThe running total of the frequencies, up to and including a category.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-518Cumulative relative frequencyThe running total of the relative frequencies; ends at 1.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-519Cumulative sumThe running total of a list of numbers; it turns weights into ranges on the line from 0 to 1.Note ML-110AdaBoost
G-520Curse of dimensionalityThe problems that appear when data has too many dimensions: lower performance and more computation.Note ML-045Curse of dimensionality
G-521CurvatureHow fast the slope of a surface changes; given in each direction by the Hessian.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-522Custom binningBinning with edges we choose from domain knowledge; also called domain-based binning.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-523Custom loss functionA loss written by the user, passed to libraries such as XGBoost with its gradient and Hessian.Note ML-127Cost-sensitive learning
G-524Customer profileA summary of what kind of buyer a customer is, built from their purchases.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-525Customer segmentationGrouping customers by their buying behaviour.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-526Cut-offsThe low and high percentiles chosen as outlier limits, such as the 1st and the 99th: values below the first or above the second are treated as outliers and trimmed or capped.Note ML-043Percentile outlier method
G-527Cutting the dendrogramDrawing a horizontal line through the dendrogram; the lines it crosses are the clusters.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-528DampingMaking an optimiser’s back-and-forth swings (oscillations) smaller: NAG brakes before it overshoots, so its path settles faster than momentum’s, though it can then stay in a small dip.Note DL-035Nesterov accelerated gradient (NAG)
G-529DashA Python library for building interactive web apps with Plotly charts.Note ML-080Logistic regression
G-542DataRecorded examples of inputs together with their outputs; a machine learning algorithm learns the pattern that links them from these examples.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-530Data analysisFinding patterns and hidden information in data, mainly by plotting graphs.Note ML-001Data mining
G-531Data augmentationEnlarging a dataset by making changed copies of its examples, such as zoomed or shifted images.Note DL-050Data augmentation
G-532Data cleaningFixing errors, gaps and inconsistencies in data.Note ML-007Poor-quality data
G-533Data engineerThe specialist who collects and organises data from company systems.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-534Data hungryNeeding a lot of data before results become reliable.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-535Data leakageInformation from the test rows reaching the model during training, for example when a scaling or feature-selection step is fitted on all the data before the split; the test scores then come out higher than the model will really do on new data.Note ML-028Data leakage
G-536Data matrixA dataset written as one matrix X: each observation’s feature vector is a row and each feature a column, so the whole dataset can be handled with matrix operations.Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-537Data miningUsing ML on data to extract patterns too hidden for graphs.Note ML-001Data mining
G-538Data pipelineA channel that carries data from one place to another, such as an API that passes a company’s data to our program.Note ML-016APIs
G-539Data preprocessing (preprocessing)Cleaning and preparing the data before training, so an algorithm can use it.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-540Data type (dtype)The kind of values a column holds, such as int64, float64 or str.Note ML-018Exploratory data analysis
G-541Data warehouseA separate store of copied company data, safe to analyse without touching the live database.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-544DatabaseA program that stores data as tables and answers queries.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-543Database serverA program that holds databases and answers queries, such as MySQL.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-545DatetimeA value pandas understands as a point in time, with date and time parts, so we can pull out parts such as the year or weekday and compute the time between two dates.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-546datetime64The pandas column type for datetimes; [us] means microsecond resolution.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-547Day of weekThe weekday as a number, Monday = 0 to Sunday = 6 (.dt.dayofweek).Note ML-033Date and time features
G-548DBSCANA clustering method that groups points lying in crowded (dense) regions and labels lonely points as noise. The name stands for density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-549ddofThe NumPy and pandas argument that sets the number subtracted from n in the variance’s denominator: ddof=1 divides by n−1 (sample variance), ddof=0 by n. NumPy defaults to 0, pandas to 1.Note MA-006Variance
G-550De Morgan’s lawTwo rules for “not” over “or” and “and”: “neither A nor B” is “not A and not B”, (A∪B)c=Ac∩Bc; “not both” is “at least one fails”, (A∩B)c=Ac∪Bc.Note MA-013Venn diagrams and contingency tables
G-551Dead neuronA node whose output is 0 for every input; it gets no updates and stays that way.Note DL-028Dying ReLU problem
G-552Dead zoneThe range of S (how strongly the data pulls the slope away from 0) for which Lasso’s best slope is exactly 0: inside it the penalty wins, which is how Lasso removes features.Note ML-067Lasso regression
G-553Decay factor βIn momentum, the share of the previous update (the velocity) kept at each step; 0 gives plain gradient descent, usually 0.9.Note DL-034SGD with momentum
G-554DecilesThe 10th, 20th, …, 90th percentiles: cuts into 10 groups.Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-555Decision boundaryA line or curve that separates the classes in classification.Note ML-006Decision surface and boundary
G-556Decision nodeA node in the middle of a tree that asks a question and splits again.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-557Decision regionThe part of the input space in which a model predicts a given class.Note ML-078Softmax regression
G-558Decision rule (SVM)How a trained SVM labels a new point u: by which side of the separating line it falls on, predicting +1 if w⋅u+b≥0 and −1 otherwise.Note ML-087Support vector machines
G-559Decision stumpA decision tree with maximum depth 1: one question, two regions. Too weak alone, it is AdaBoost’s usual weak learner.Note ML-109AdaBoost
G-560Decision surfaceA plot colouring every point of the input space by the class the model would predict there.Note ML-085Decision surface and boundary
G-561Decision treeA model that predicts by asking a chain of questions about the input columns: nested if-else conditions.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-562DecisionTreeRegressorscikit-learn’s regression tree: a decision tree whose leaves predict a number, the mean target of the training rows in the leaf, instead of a class. It is used exactly like DecisionTreeClassifier.Note ML-093Regression trees
G-564DecoderThe part of a seq2seq model that writes the output sequence.Note DL-067Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-563Decoder blockOne layer of the decoder: masked self-attention, cross-attention and a feed-forward network, each followed by add and norm; the decoder stacks 6.Note DL-084Transformer decoder
G-565Decoder-only transformerA transformer with the encoder removed, so no cross-attention: a stack of blocks, each with masked self-attention and an MLP, that guesses the next token at every position. GPT is built this way.Note DL-087Decoder-only GPT
G-566Decoding notationShrinking a formula’s indices to two or three cases and writing every case out by hand.Note MA-002How to learn the maths for ML
G-567Deep belief networkA many-layered network from Hinton and colleagues (2006) whose starting weights were set by unsupervised pre-training, one layer at a time; its success led the field to be renamed deep learning.Note DL-003Types of neural networks
G-568Deep Learning (DL)Machine Learning that uses neural networks with many layers; finds features by itself.Note ML-002Deep learning
G-569Deep LSTM, deep GRUTwo or more LSTM (or GRU) layers stacked on top of each other: a deep RNN whose recurrent layers are LSTM or GRU layers.Note DL-065Deep (stacked) RNNs
G-570Deep network (deep neural network)A neural network with many hidden layers.Note DL-002Neural networks
G-572Deep reinforcement learningReinforcement learning (an agent learning from rewards by trial and error) that uses deep neural networks; it raised the skill of game-playing programs.Note DL-003Reinforcement learning
G-573Deep RNN (stacked RNN)An RNN with two or more recurrent layers stacked on top of each other, all unfolded through time.Note DL-065Deep (stacked) RNNs
G-574Default directionThe side of a split that rows with a missing value follow. XGBoost tries sending them left and then right and keeps the side with the larger gain, so trees handle missing values without filling them in.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-575Define-by-runBuilding the search space while the objective function runs, so it can depend on earlier choices.Note ML-128Optuna
G-576Degradation problemDeeper plain networks reaching a higher training error than shallower ones.Note DL-081Residual connections and add & norm
G-577DegreeThe highest power used in a polynomial, such as 2 for x2. It sets the model’s complexity: a higher degree lets the curve bend more, and too high a degree overfits.Note ML-060Polynomial regression
G-578Degrees of freedomThe number of deviations free to vary, n−1 for a sample of size n; it sets the shape of the t-distribution (its parameter).Note MA-037Student’s t-distribution
G-579Delivery routingPlanning the most efficient route for deliveries.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-580Demand forecastingPredicting how much of something will be needed, where and when.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-581Dendrites, nucleus, axonThe parts of a brain neuron that receive signals (dendrites), process them (nucleus) and send the result on (axon); in a perceptron they match the inputs with weights, the summation and activation, and the output.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-582DendrogramA tree showing which rows (or columns) were joined as similar, and in what order.Note ML-020Hierarchical clustering
G-583Dense (fully connected) layerA layer whose every node receives the output of every node in the layer before.Note DL-011ANN for classification
G-584Dense region, sparse regionAn area with many points close together; an area with few points.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-585Dense representationA short vector of real numbers, most of them non-zero, such as a word embedding; unlike a long, mostly-zero one-hot vector, every number carries information.Note DL-057Word embeddings
G-586Density estimationWorking out, from observed data, how likely each value of a random variable is: estimating its probability density function (PDF).Note MA-023Density estimation
G-587Density plotA histogram with a smooth KDE curve drawn along the tops of its bars, so the shape of a numerical column’s distribution is easier to see.Note ML-019Kernel density estimation (KDE)
G-588Density-based clusteringClustering that finds dense regions of points separated by sparse regions.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-589Density-connectedTwo points linked by a chain of core points with every step at most eps, so we can walk from one to the other through the dense region; DBSCAN puts density-connected points in the same cluster.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-590Dependent eventsEvents that are not independent: knowing one changes the probability of the other.Note MA-016Independent and mutually exclusive events
G-591Dependent variableAnother name for the target, the output y that a model predicts; it is called dependent because it depends on the features.Note ML-012Supervised learning
G-592Deployment (deploy, model deployment)Moving a model from development to production: putting it on a server so users can reach it.Note ML-004Deployment
G-594DepthThe number of questions on the longest path from a tree’s root to a leaf.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-595DerivativeThe slope of a function at a point: how fast the output changes as the input changes there. It is zero at the lowest point of a smooth curve, which is how training finds a minimum.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-596Descriptive statisticsNumbers that summarise data, such as count, mean, spread and percentiles.Note MA-004Descriptive statistics
G-597Design matrix (X)The data as a matrix, one row per observation and one column per feature, plus a first column of 1s; the 1s multiply the intercept, so it is treated like any other coefficient.Note ML-053Normal equation
G-598DeterminantThe factor by which a matrix scales areas (volumes in 3D); 0 when it squishes space into a lower dimension.Note MA-056Determinant
G-599Development environmentOur own machine, where we build and train a model.Note ML-004Batch (offline) learning
G-600Diabetes datasetscikit-learn’s built-in data of 442 patients, 10 standardised inputs, and disease progression one year later.Note ML-054Multiple linear regression
G-601Diagonal matrixA matrix with zeros everywhere off the diagonal; it scales each axis by its own factor.Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-602DiagonalisationRewriting a matrix so that, seen along its eigenvectors, it only stretches each axis: A=PDP−1, where P holds its eigenvectors and D is diagonal. This makes its powers easy to compute.Note MA-056Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-603Dictionary (Python)A lookup table from keys to values, written {key: value}.Note ML-016APIs
G-604Difference quotientThe average slope of a function over a step h: the change in output divided by the change in input, (f(x+h)−f(x))/h, the slope of the secant line. Shrinking h towards 0 gives the derivative.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-606DifferentiableHaving a derivative (one clear slope) at a point, or at every point; the absolute value ∣m∣ is not, at its corner m=0. Gradient descent needs a differentiable loss.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-605Differentiable lossA loss function whose derivative exists at every point, so it can be minimised with derivatives.Note ML-115Gradient boosting
G-607Differential entropyHow uncertain a continuous variable is (the entropy of a continuous variable): higher for a more spread-out distribution.Note ML-091Entropy, information gain and Gini
G-608DifferentiationFinding the slope of a curve at each point; the derivative of the CDF is the PDF.Note MA-022Derivatives of one variable
G-610DimensionOne feature (input column) of the data, seen as one axis of the space the observations live in: 10 features give 10 dimensions. A tensor’s dimensions mean something else, its number of axes.Note ML-003Dimensionality reduction
G-609Dimension of a vectorThe dimension of the space it lives in: its number of components.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-612DimensionalityThe number of features (columns) in the data; one-hot encoding raises it by one column per category, and too high a dimensionality brings the curse of dimensionality.Note ML-026Curse of dimensionality
G-611Dimensionality reductionReducing the number of input columns while keeping the information.Note ML-045Dimensionality reduction
G-613DirectionThe way an arrow (vector) points, regardless of its length. In a word embedding, meaning lives in directions: the arrow from “man” to “woman” points roughly the same way as the one from “uncle” to “aunt”.Note DL-072Meaning as direction in embedding space
G-614Directional derivativeHow steeply a function rises when we step in a chosen direction, given by a unit vector u, instead of only along an axis. It is the dot product ∇f⋅u.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-615Dirty dataData with errors, gaps, duplicates or inconsistencies.Note ML-009Poor-quality data
G-616Discrete dataNumerical data that takes only separate values, usually counts.Note MA-004Discrete and continuous data
G-617Discrete random variableA random variable that takes separate values, such as a die’s face.Note MA-020Random variables
G-618Discrete uniform distributionA discrete distribution in which every possible value is equally likely, such as a fair die.Note MA-021Uniform distribution
G-619DiscretizationTurning a continuous column into a discrete one by cutting its range into intervals.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-620DiscriminatorIn a GAN, the network that judges whether data is real or fake.Note DL-003Types of neural networks
G-623DistanceA number measuring how far apart two points are; small distance = similar.Note ML-006Instance-based learning
G-621Distance weight (nan-Euclidean)In the nan-Euclidean distance, the factor that scales the sum up: the total number of features divided by the number present in both observations. It makes up for the skipped features, so observations with many gaps do not look too close.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-622Distance weightingEach neighbour counts in proportion to 1 / its distance, so nearer rows count more.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-624distance_thresholdHeight at which AgglomerativeClustering stops merging, instead of a fixed number of clusters.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-625Distributed computingSharing one job between several machines (nodes), coordinated by a master node.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-626DistributionHow a column’s values spread over their range.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-627Distributive lawThe rule that multiplying a sum gives the same result as adding the separate products, a⋅(b+c)=a⋅b+a⋅c; the dot product obeys it, so a dot product with a sum can be split into two.Note MA-050Dot product
G-628Diverge (divergence)To move further away with each step: the updates overshoot more and more, so the loss grows instead of shrinking.Note ML-056Gradient descent
G-630Divisive clusteringTop-down hierarchical clustering: start with one cluster and split repeatedly.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-632DomainThe set of allowed inputs of a function.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-631Domain knowledgeKnowledge of the field the data comes from, such as medicine, property or shipping; it tells us which features make sense and which new ones would help.Note ML-022Feature engineering
G-633DonorA row that has a value in the column being filled, so it can be a neighbour.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-2230Dot plotA frequency table drawn with one dot per observation, stacked over its value.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-634Dot productMultiplying two vectors entry by entry and adding the products, uTx, which gives one number. It is large when the vectors point the same way, so it measures similarity and gives projections.Note MA-050Dot product
G-635Dot scoreLuong’s simplest attention score: the dot product of the decoder state and an encoder state, si⊤​hj​, large when the two point the same way. It needs no learned parameters, but both states must have the same size.Note DL-070Luong (multiplicative) attention
G-636DownsamplingReducing the height and width of a feature map.Note DL-044Pooling
G-2167Draft / confirmedThe two states of a Concept on the Course map: draft means no written Note teaches it yet (shown faint, checked against its source when the Note is written); confirmed means a written Note already teaches it.Course map
G-637dropnaThe pandas method that drops rows (or columns) with missing values.Note ML-034Complete case analysis
G-639DropoutSwitching off a random set of input and hidden nodes at every training step, to reduce overfitting.Note DL-024Dropout
G-638Dropout rate (p)The probability that each node of a layer is switched off in a training step.Note DL-024Dropout
G-640dtreevizA Python library that draws decision trees with the training data shown at every node.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-642Dual problemA second problem that looks for the highest guaranteed floor under a constrained minimum. Each price λ≥0 on the constraints gives a floor, the lowest value of the Lagrangian, D(λ)=minx​L; the dual problem maximises D, and a feasible point that reaches the floor is the best.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-643Dual vectorThe one vector whose dot product does the same job as a given linear transformation from vectors to a number; for example, a linear model’s weight vector is the dual vector of its scoring function.Note MA-055Linear transformations and matrices
G-644DualityThe one-to-one match between vectors and linear maps that turn a vector into a number: every such map is a dot product with exactly one vector. So a vector can be read as a scoring function, and a scoring function as a vector.Note MA-055Dot product
G-645Dummy copy W(t)A copy of a weight that an RNN reuses at every time step, one copy for step t only; the shared weight’s gradient is the sum over the copies.Note DL-059Backpropagation through time (BPTT)
G-647Dummy variableOne of the 0/1 columns made by one-hot encoding; each marks whether a row belongs to one category, so a model can use a categorical column as numbers.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-646Dummy variable trapThe problem caused by keeping all n dummy columns of a category: they always add up to 1, so any one can be calculated from the others (multicollinearity) and a linear model’s weights become unstable. Dropping one column (n−1 kept) avoids it.Note ML-026Multicollinearity
G-648Duplicate rowA row identical to another row in every column. Duplicates give some examples extra weight and distort what a model learns, so we check for them before any analysis.Note ML-018Poor-quality data
G-649Durbin-Watson statisticA number from 0 to 4 that checks whether a regression’s residuals are linked to the residuals next to them (autocorrelation); about 2 means no such link.Note ML-055Assumptions of linear regression
G-650Dying ReLU problemReLU nodes ending up with a negative weighted sum for every input, so they output 0 and stop learning.Note DL-028Dying ReLU problem
G-652Dynamic programmingSolving a problem by storing the answer to each overlapping sub-problem the first time it is computed and looking it up afterwards, so no work is repeated; memoization is one form of it.Note DL-019Memoization
G-653Dynamic search spaceA search space in which some hyperparameters exist only for some values of another, such as the algorithm; the tuner then suggests only settings that make sense for the choice already made.Note ML-128Optuna
G-654E-stepThe expectation step of the EM algorithm: using the current parameters, give every point its responsibilities (the probability that it came from each component), a soft assignment that the M-step then uses.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-655Eager learningLearning that does all its work up front, building a model from the training data before any question arrives; another name for model-based learning and the opposite of lazy learning.Note ML-006Model-based learning
G-656Early stoppingStopping training when the score on held-out data is best, before full convergence; this keeps coefficients small, so it also acts as regularisation.Note ML-057Early stopping
G-657Eckart–Young theoremThe theorem that the truncated SVD (keeping the k largest singular values) is the closest rank k matrix to A, so it is the best way to compress A to rank k; its spectral error is σk+1​.Note MA-059Low-rank approximation (truncated SVD)
G-658Economy rateA cricket feature built from raw totals: a bowler’s runs conceded per over. It rates bowlers better than total runs; a lower economy rate is better.Note ML-044Feature construction and splitting
G-661EdgeIn an image, a place where the intensity changes sharply, such as where a dark region meets a light one. Finding edges is the first job of a CNN’s filters.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-659Edge detector (filter)A filter whose feature map is large along edges of one direction.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-2263Edge detector (hidden node)A node whose weights are positive on a strip of pixels and negative around it, so it switches on when that strip holds a stroke.Note DL-009Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-660Edge TPUA small Google chip for running networks on drones, watches and glasses.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-662Effective learning rateThe learning rate a parameter actually gets after AdaGrad’s division: η/(vt​​+ϵ).Note DL-036AdaGrad
G-663Eigen-decompositionFinding all the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix. In PCA it is done on the covariance matrix: the eigenvectors give the directions of the principal components and the eigenvalues the variance along each.Note ML-047PCA
G-664EigenbasisA basis made of eigenvectors of a matrix. Seen in this basis the matrix only scales each basis vector, so it becomes a diagonal matrix, which makes powers such as Ak easy to compute.Note MA-056Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-665EigenvalueThe number by which a matrix stretches or shrinks one of its eigenvectors: Av=λv. In PCA, the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix are the variances along the principal components.Note ML-047Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-666EigenvectorA non-zero vector that a matrix only stretches or shrinks, without turning it off its own line: Av=λv. In PCA, the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix are the directions of the principal components.Note ML-047Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-667Elastic Net regression (Elastic Net)Linear regression whose loss gets both the L2 (ridge) and the L1 (lasso) penalty, each with its own strength. It shrinks the coefficients and can set some to 0, so we need not choose between ridge and lasso in advance.Note ML-068Elastic Net
G-669ElasticNetCVscikit-learn’s Elastic Net that picks alpha and l1_ratio by cross-validation.Note ML-068Elastic Net
G-670Elbow curveA plot of WCSS (how far points sit from their own cluster centre) against the number of clusters k; the point where it bends is used to choose k.Note ML-122Elbow method and WCSS
G-671Elbow methodChoosing k at the point where the elbow curve bends from steep to flat.Note ML-122Elbow method and WCSS
G-672Elbow pointThe k where the elbow curve bends, after which adding clusters barely lowers WCSS; it is the number of clusters the elbow method picks.Note ML-122Elbow method and WCSS
G-2277Element-wise (Hadamard) product ⊙Multiplying two grids of the same shape cell by cell, so each output cell depends only on the matching input cells; backpropagation uses it to apply a mask or a local slope to every cell at once.Note DL-048Backpropagation in a CNN
G-673Elongated bowlA loss surface stretched far more in one direction than another, with long elliptical contours, as a sparse feature produces. Gradient descent on it wastes steps moving along the steep direction and crawls along the flat one.Note DL-036AdaGrad
G-674ELUExponential linear unit: an activation that equals ReLU for positive inputs and follows a smooth exponential curve levelling off at −α for negative ones, so negative inputs still give a gradient and nodes do not die. Formula: z for z≥0, α(ez−1) for z<0.Note DL-028Leaky ReLU, PReLU, ELU and SELU
G-675EM algorithm (expectation maximization)A method for finding the maximum likelihood when some variables are hidden (latent): it repeats two steps, an E-step and an M-step, until the fit settles.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-677EmbeddingA learned vector representing a user, item or word, compared with others by dot products.Note DL-057Word embeddings
G-676Embedding vectorThe list of numbers that represents one word, drawn as an arrow from the origin; words used in similar ways get nearby arrows, so a model can compare words through their vectors.Note DL-076Word embeddings
G-678Empirical (experimental) probabilityThe share of trials in which an event happened, counted from data. It estimates the probability when it cannot be worked out from the sample space.Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-679Empirical CDF (ECDF)The share of a sample’s values at or below x; a step-function estimate of the CDF.Note MA-027Cumulative distribution function (CDF)
G-680encodeThe KBinsDiscretizer parameter choosing ordinal (bin numbers) or one-hot output.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-682EncoderThe part of a seq2seq model that reads the input sequence and summarises it.Note DL-067Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-681Encoder blockOne layer of the transformer encoder: multi-head attention and then a feed-forward network, each followed by add and norm. It turns each word’s vector into a more context-aware one; the encoder stacks 6 of them.Note DL-081Transformer encoder
G-683Encoder-only / decoder-only transformerA transformer that keeps only the encoder (BERT) or only the decoder (GPT).Note DL-071Transformer
G-684Encoder–decoder attentionThe paper’s name for cross-attention, also called source attention: the decoder’s attention layer whose queries come from the output sentence and whose keys and values come from the encoder, so each word being written can draw on the input sentence.Note DL-083Cross-attention
G-685EncodingTwo senses: the rulebook that maps text characters to stored bytes (Video 15); or turning categories into numbers (categorical encoding, Video 26).Note ML-014Encoding categorical data
G-686End of distribution imputationFilling every gap in a numerical column with a value at the far edge of its distribution, μ±3σ for a normal column or Q3​+1.5IQR for a skewed one, so the model can tell which rows were missing.Note ML-035Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
G-687End-to-end productA complete product, from raw data to software that users use.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-688EndpointOne address of an API that returns one kind of data.Note ML-016APIs
G-690EnsembleSeveral trained models whose predictions are combined.Note ML-095Ensemble learning
G-689Ensemble learningCombining several models into one stronger model.Note ML-009Ensemble learning
G-691EntropyA measure of disorder (impurity) of the class labels in a node, −∑pi​log2​pi​: 0 when all rows are one class, 1 for a 50/50 two-class node. A decision tree splits where entropy drops most (highest information gain).Note ML-091Entropy, information gain and Gini
G-694EnvironmentIn reinforcement learning, the world the agent acts in, such as the road or a game board; it rewards or punishes each action, and the agent learns from that.Note ML-003Reinforcement learning
G-692Environment fileA file (environment.yml) listing an environment’s name, channel and every package with its exact version, so anyone can rebuild the same environment and get the same results.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-693Environment variableA named value stored on the computer outside the code and read with os.environ; used to keep secrets such as API keys out of notebooks that get shared.Note ML-016APIs
G-695EpigraphThe region on and above a function’s graph; convex exactly when the function is convex.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-696EpochOne full update of the parameters using the whole training set.Note DL-005Perceptron
G-697eps (epsilon)The radius of the neighbourhood DBSCAN examines around each point.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-698eps-neighbourhoodAll points within distance eps of a point (the circle of radius eps around it); DBSCAN counts the points in it to judge how dense the data is there.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-699Equal frequency binningBinning into bins holding the same number of rows, with the quantiles as edges; also called quantile binning.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-700Equal variances (homogeneity of variance)The assumption that two populations have the same variance, σ12​=σ22​. Student’s t-test needs it; Welch’s t-test does not, and Levene’s test checks it.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-701Equal width binningBinning into bins of the same width, (max−min)/k; also called uniform binning.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-702Equally likely outcomesOutcomes that all have the same probability, such as the faces of a fair die.Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-703Equation of a hyperplaneOne equation for a flat boundary in any number of dimensions, a line in 2D, a plane in 3D, a hyperplane beyond: wTx+w0​=0.Note MA-051Equation of a hyperplane
G-704EquiprobableEqually likely: every outcome has the same probability, as the six faces of a fair die, so each has probability 1 divided by the number of outcomes.Note MA-020Probability distributions
G-705Error (residual)The gap between an actual value and the model’s prediction on one data point: actual minus predicted.Note ML-049Best-fit line and squared error
G-707errors=“coerce”The pd.to_numeric option that turns values it cannot convert into NaN instead of stopping.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-708Estimated PMFEach value’s share of many repeated trials, used as its probability.Note MA-021Probability mass function (PMF)
G-709estimatorThe scikit-learn bagging setting that names the model to train many copies of (the base model); formerly base_estimator.Note ML-100Bagging
G-710estimators_features_The column numbers each trained base model was given.Note ML-100Bagging
G-711estimators_samples_The row numbers each trained base model was given.Note ML-100Bagging
G-712Eta (η)XGBoost’s name for the learning rate; default 0.3.Note ML-118XGBoost
G-713eta0The starting learning rate in SGDRegressor.Note ML-058Stochastic gradient descent
G-714ETLExtract, transform, load: copying data from source systems into a warehouse.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-715Euclidean distanceThe straight-line distance between two points.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-716Euler’s number eA fixed number, about 2.71828, that appears in the Poisson PMF.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-717EventA set of outcomes, such as “the sum is at most 10”.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-718EvidenceThe overall chance of seeing what we observed, counted over every possible hypothesis, written P(E). Bayes’ theorem divides by it: posterior = likelihood × prior / evidence.Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-719Exact greedy algorithmFinding a split by trying the midpoint between every pair of neighbouring sorted values.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-720Excess kurtosisKurtosis minus 3, so a normal distribution scores 0.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-721Exhaustive eventsEvents that together cover the whole sample space, so at least one always happens.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-722Expected complete-data log-likelihood QA score for how well the model explains the data if we also knew which group made each point: the log-likelihood of the observations together with their hidden labels, averaged over the labels with the responsibilities, written Q. The M-step of EM maximises it, which never lowers the real log-likelihood.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-723Expected count EThe number of rows a category or cell would hold on average if the null hypothesis H0​ were true.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-724Expected improvementA score that picks which point Bayesian optimisation tries next: how much better than the best score so far a candidate point is expected to be, judged from the surrogate model’s predicted mean and uncertainty. The point with the highest expected improvement is tried next.Note ML-128Bayesian optimisation
G-725Expected value E[X]The average value we would get over many repeats: each possible value times its probability, added up (the probability-weighted average of a random variable). Also called the long-run mean and written μ.Note MA-012Expected value and variance of a random variable
G-726Expert systemEarly AI: a human expert’s knowledge written as rules, plus a program that applies them.Note ML-002Symbolic AI and expert systems
G-728Explained varianceHow much of the data’s spread one principal component keeps: the variance of the data along that component, equal to its eigenvalue.Note ML-048PCA
G-727Explained variance ratioThe share of the data’s total spread that one principal component keeps: its eigenvalue divided by the sum of all eigenvalues (its share of the total variance). Adding these shares from the largest down tells us how many components to keep.Note ML-048PCA
G-729explained_variance_How much of the data’s spread each principal component keeps (its eigenvalue), stored on a fitted PCA, largest first.Note ML-048PCA
G-730Explicit programmingA human writing out every rule the computer follows. ML avoids it.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-731Exploding gradientGradients growing huge as they pass back through many layers, making updates erratic.Note DL-018Exploding gradient and gradient clipping
G-732Exploratory data analysis (EDA)Exploring data with summaries and plots to find patterns.Note ML-009Exploratory data analysis
G-733Exponential distributionThe pattern of waiting times between random events: short waits are common and long waits rare (a right-skewed continuous distribution).Note MA-071Exponential distribution
G-734Exponential timeWork that is multiplied by a constant factor with every step of the input size.Note DL-019Memoization
