G-735Exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA)A running average in which recent values count most and older values count less and less, updated as Vt​=βVt−1​+(1−β)θt​. Momentum and Adam use it to average the gradients.Note DL-033Exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA)
G-736export_graphvizscikit-learn function that writes a trained decision tree as text in Graphviz’s DOT format, which Graphviz then draws as a tree diagram.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-737export_textscikit-learn function that prints a trained tree as indented text.Note ML-104Bagging
G-738ExtrapolationPredicting for inputs outside the range of the training data.Note ML-049Simple linear regression
G-739F distributionThe shape that a ratio of two independent spreads (variances) follows: a right-skewed continuous distribution with two degrees-of-freedom parameters. ANOVA compares its F statistic with this distribution to get a p-value.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-740F statisticOne number that compares how far apart the group means are with how spread out the values are inside each group: the variance between the group means divided by the variance within the groups, MSB/MSW. One-way ANOVA computes it; a large F means the group means differ more than the spread inside the groups would explain.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-741f-stringText starting with f in which {name} is replaced by a value.Note ML-016APIs
G-742F-testA check of whether two groups have the same spread, made from the ratio of the two sample variances (a hypothesis test of equal population variances); an alternative to Levene’s test.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-743F1 scoreOne number that combines precision and recall as their harmonic mean, 2PR/(P+R); it is high only when both are high, so it is used when both kinds of mistake matter.Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-744Facet gridThe same plot repeated side by side, one panel per category of another column.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-745Fact (here)An athlete’s sport, as the model’s ranking of 10 sports after “⟨name⟩ plays the sport of”.Note DL-089MLP blocks as fact storage
G-746Fail to reject H0​The decision that the evidence against the null hypothesis H0​ is not strong enough to drop it; it does not prove H0​.Note MA-038Hypothesis testing: null and alternative
G-747False negative (FN)Predicted negative, but actually positive; a Type II error.Note ML-075Confusion matrix
G-748False positive (FP)Predicted positive, but actually negative; a Type I error.Note ML-075Confusion matrix
G-749False positive rate (FPR)The fraction of real negatives the model wrongly flags.Note ML-077ROC curve and AUC
G-750Family sizeSibSp + Parch + 1: the number of people in a passenger’s travelling family.Note ML-044Feature construction and splitting
G-751Family typeFamily size grouped into alone, small family (2 to 4) and large family (5 or more).Note ML-044Feature construction and splitting
G-752Familywise error rateThe chance of at least one false alarm (Type I error) when running several tests: 1−(1−α)m for m tests, each at significance level α.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-753Famous probability distributionsCommon named shapes such as normal, uniform, binomial and Poisson.Note MA-020Probability distributions
G-754Fan-inThe number of inputs coming into a node, equal to the size of the previous layer. Xavier and He initialisation use it to set the spread of the starting weights.Note DL-030Xavier and He initialisation
G-755Fan-outThe number of outputs leaving a node, equal to the size of the next layer. Xavier initialisation uses it, with fan-in, to set the spread of the starting weights.Note DL-030Xavier and He initialisation
G-756Fashion-MNISTA dataset of 28 × 28 greyscale images of 10 kinds of clothing, in the same format as MNIST.Note DL-046Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-757Fat tail (heavy tail)A tail that falls to zero slowly, so extreme values are relatively common.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-758Favourable outcomeAn outcome that belongs to the event we are measuring.Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-759Feasible regionAll the points that obey every rule (constraint) of an optimisation problem; the answer must be one of them.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-772FeatureOne piece of information about each example that a model uses (e.g. a student’s CGPA).Note ML-002Features
G-760Feature constructionCreating a new column by hand from existing ones, e.g. rooms + washrooms into area.Note ML-022Feature construction and splitting
G-761Feature engineeringChoosing, removing and creating input columns (features) so that the model gets the information it needs in a form it can use.Note ML-009Feature engineering
G-762Feature extractionLetting an algorithm such as PCA produce new columns from the existing ones (compare feature construction, where we make them by hand).Note ML-022Feature extraction
G-764Feature importanceHow much a column helped a tree: its share of all the impurity reduction (how much purer the nodes became) achieved by the tree’s splits; the shares add up to 1. It shows which columns the tree relied on and helps with feature selection.Note ML-093Feature importance
G-763Feature importance (weights)Reading the size of a weight as how much its input matters, fair only on scaled inputs.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-765Feature map (ϕ)A rule that gives each point extra coordinates built from its own values, such as ϕ(x)=(x,x2), moving the data into a higher-dimensional space. Data that no straight line can separate becomes linearly separable there.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-766Feature map (CNN)The grid of numbers a filter produces; large where the filter’s pattern is present.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-767Feature scaling (scaling)Putting columns on the same scale, so no column dominates distances.Note ML-012Feature scaling
G-768Feature selectionKeeping only the useful input columns and dropping the rest.Note ML-022Feature selection
G-2219Feature spaceThe space whose axes are the features; the feature map takes the data into a higher-dimensional one.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-769Feature splittingBreaking a column that holds several facts into one column per fact.Note ML-044Feature construction and splitting
G-770Feature transformationChanging a column into a form the model can use better.Note ML-022Feature transformation
G-771Feature vectorThe vector of input values of one data point.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-773feature_importances_The value stored on a trained tree model that holds the feature importance of every column.Note ML-093Feature importance
G-775Feed-forward networkA network in which information moves only from the first layer to the last.Note DL-003Types of neural networks
G-774Feed-forward network (FFN)A small two-layer network inside each transformer block that works on each word’s vector on its own: dense layers 512 → 2048 with ReLU → 512. Attention mixes the words; this network transforms each word and adds the block’s only per-word non-linearity.Note DL-081Transformer encoder
G-776Fence (fences)A cut-off for spotting outliers in a box plot: 1.5 times the IQR (the width of the middle half of the data) beyond the box, Q1​−1.5IQR or Q3​+1.5IQR; values past it are possible outliers.Note ML-019Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-2197Fill errorThe average gap between filled values and the true values they replace, measured on values we hid on purpose.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-777Filter (kernel)A small grid of weights slid over the image; at each position it multiplies and adds, so it responds strongly where its pattern (such as an edge) appears and produces a feature map. Its depth equals the input’s number of channels.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-779Fine-tuningTraining a pre-trained model further on a small dataset for a specific task.Note DL-053Transfer learning (feature extraction and fine-tuning)
G-780First moment mt​A running average of the recent gradients in which older ones count less (an EWMA), so it estimates the gradient’s mean; written mt​. Adam uses it in its update.Note DL-038Adam
G-781First-order conditionA test for a bowl-shaped (convex) function: a differentiable function is convex exactly when every tangent plane lies on or below its graph.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-782Fisher’s exact testA test for small 2 by 2 count tables that computes the p-value exactly instead of approximating it; used when expected counts fall below 5.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-783fit / transformLearn the scaler’s numbers from the training set / apply them to any data.Note ML-023Standardization
G-784fit_predictTrains a clustering model and returns the cluster of every row.Note ML-123K-means
G-785fit_transformLearns the numbers from the data and applies them in one call (fit, then transform); used on the training set only.Note ML-027Column transformer
G-786Fitting a distributionChoosing a family of distributions for data, then choosing its parameters.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-787Five-number summaryThe five numbers that describe a column’s centre and spread: minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. A box plot draws them.Note ML-019Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-788Flatten layerA layer that reshapes a multi-dimensional input into one dimension; no parameters.Note DL-012ANN for classification
G-789FlatteningReshaping a matrix into one long vector so that derivatives stay matrices.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-790FLOPOne floating-point operation; training cost is counted in FLOPs.Note DL-086The transformer end to end (capstone)
G-2227FoldOne of the equal blocks the data is cut into for cross-validation; each fold is the test block once.Note ML-106Cross-validation
G-791For loopCode that repeats once for each item of a collection.Note ML-014CSV files
G-792Forest-level hyperparametersThe settings that shape the forest itself: n_estimators, max_features, bootstrap, max_samples.Note ML-105Random forest
G-793Forget gate (ft​)The LSTM gate that decides what to erase from the memory (cell state): a sigmoid layer whose outputs, between 0 and 1, scale each entry of the previous cell state ct−1​.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-795Format stringA pattern such as "%d/%m/%Y" telling pd.to_datetime how dates are written.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-796Forward and backward RNNThe left-to-right and the right-to-left halves of a bidirectional RNN.Note DL-066Bidirectional RNNs
G-797Forward propagationPassing one row of inputs through the network, layer by layer, to get the prediction.Note DL-010Forward propagation
G-798Forward selectionFeature selection that starts empty and adds the best column at a time.Note ML-022Feature selection
G-799Four fundamental subspacesFour sets of directions tied to every matrix that show what it does: which input directions it uses, which it squashes to zero, which outputs it can reach and which it never reaches. They are the row space, null space, column space and left null space.Note MA-058Singular value decomposition
G-800FPGAA reprogrammable chip: fast and low-power, but expensive.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-801FrameOne image in a video.Note ML-010Tensors
G-802Framing an ML problemTurning a business problem into a precise ML task that can be built and measured.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-804Fraud detectionSpotting dishonest transactions; here the outliers are what we want to find.Note ML-040Outliers
G-805FreezeMark a layer’s weights as not trainable, so that training leaves them unchanged.Note DL-053Transfer learning (feature extraction and fine-tuning)
G-808FrequencyHow many times a value or category occurs.Note ML-019Frequency tables
G-806Frequency and wavelengthHow fast a wave repeats, and the distance after which it repeats; one is the inverse of the other.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-807Frequency distribution tableA table of each value or category with the number of times it occurs.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-809Frobenius normOne number for the size of a matrix: the square root of the sum of all its squared entries, also equal to ∑σi2​​ over its singular values σi​.Note MA-059Low-rank approximation (truncated SVD)
G-810Full SVDThe version of the SVD that keeps every column of U and V, so both are square and Σ has the same shape as A, with the singular values on its diagonal padded with zeros. It gives complete orthonormal bases for both the input and the output space.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-813Fully grown treeA tree split until every leaf is pure; usually overfits.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-814funcThe FunctionTransformer parameter that holds the function to apply.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-816FunctionA rule that assigns exactly one output to every input, written f:R→R, x↦f(x).Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-815Function of several variablesA function that takes several numbers in (a vector of n inputs) and gives one number out, f:Rn→R; a loss that depends on many weights is one.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-817Function, lambdaA named reusable piece of code (def), and a one-line unnamed one.Note ML-014Function transformer
G-818Functional APIThe Keras way of building a model as a graph of layers, by calling each layer on the output of the one before; unlike a Sequential model it allows several inputs or outputs, branches and skip connections.Note DL-054Keras functional API
G-819FunctionTransformerscikit-learn’s class that applies any function we give it to the data.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-820Gain (XGBoost)How much a split improves an XGBoost tree: the similarity scores of the two children minus the similarity score of the parent; the split with the largest gain is chosen.Note ML-118XGBoost
G-2213Gambler’s fallacyThe mistaken belief that after a run of heads, tails is “due”; independent tosses have no memory.Note MA-016Independent and mutually exclusive events
G-821Gamma (γ, min_split_loss)A setting that stops weak splits in XGBoost: a split is kept only if its gain exceeds gamma; default 0.Note ML-118XGBoost
G-823gamma (RBF kernel)How far one point’s influence reaches in the RBF kernel; large gamma gives tighter boundaries.Note ML-090Kernel trick
G-822Gamma distributionA family of right-skewed continuous distributions with a shape and a scale parameter.Note MA-033Central limit theorem
G-824Garbage in, garbage outBad input data always gives bad results.Note ML-007Poor-quality data
G-825GateA part of the LSTM cell that controls what moves into, out of, or along the cell state.Note DL-061LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-826Gated recurrent unit (GRU)An RNN architecture with one memory (the hidden state) and two gates, reset and update.Note DL-064GRU (gated recurrent unit)
G-827Gaussian distributionAnother name for the normal distribution: the symmetric, bell-shaped continuous distribution set by its mean and standard deviation, used to model many measurements.Note MA-024Normal distribution
G-828Gaussian kernelIn kernel density estimation, a bump shaped like the normal curve placed on every data point; adding the bumps gives a smooth estimate of the density. It is the usual default kernel.Note MA-023Kernel density estimation (KDE)
G-829Gaussian mixture model (GMM)A model for data made of several overlapping groups: one normal curve per group, combined as a weighted sum ∑k​πk​N(x∣μk​,σk2​). Each point is shared among the curves by probabilities instead of being given to one group.Note MA-073Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
G-830Gaussian Naive BayesNaive Bayes that models each numerical input as normally distributed within each class.Note ML-084Naive Bayes
G-831Gaussian noiseRandom errors that follow a bell curve centred on 0, N(0,σ2). Assuming them and maximising the likelihood (MLE) gives the squared-error loss.Note MA-072Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-832Gaussian processA model that predicts a value and its uncertainty at every point; a common choice of surrogate, the stand-in model that Bayesian optimisation searches.Note ML-128Bayesian optimisation
G-833GaussianNBscikit-learn’s Gaussian Naive Bayes.Note ML-084Naive Bayes
G-834GELUA smooth activation function that multiplies each input x by Φ(x), the chance that a standard normal value is below x: xΦ(x) (Gaussian Error Linear Unit). GPT’s MLPs use it.Note DL-087GELU activation
G-836General contextual embeddingA word vector that changes with the surrounding words but is computed without any learned parameters, so it is the same for every task.Note DL-074Contextual embeddings
G-837General scoreA way to score how well a decoder state si​ matches an encoder state hj​ through a learned matrix, si⊤​Wa​hj​ (Luong’s general score). It lets the two states have different sizes and lets the model learn which directions of similarity matter.Note DL-070Bahdanau (additive) attention
G-838Generalisation (generalise)How well a model performs on new data it was not trained on.Note ML-070Overfitting
G-840Generative adversarial network (GAN)A generator and a discriminator competing, so that the generator learns to create realistic new data.Note DL-003Types of neural networks
G-841Generative AIModels that create new content such as text, images, code or video.Note DL-071Transformer
G-842Generative processA step-by-step recipe that produces data from a model.Note MA-073Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
G-843GeneratorThe GAN network that creates new data.Note DL-003Types of neural networks
G-844Geometric meanAn average for values that multiply, such as growth factors: multiply the n values together and take the n-th root.Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-2248Geometric understandingKnowing what a computation means as a picture: which tool fits, why it works, how to read the result.Note MA-002How to learn the maths for ML
G-845get_dummiespandas function that turns each category into its own 0/1 column (one-hot encoding); drop_first=True keeps n−1 of them.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-846get_feature_names_outOneHotEncoder method that returns the names of the new columns.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-847Gini impurityA number for how mixed the class labels in a node are (impurity), 1−∑pi2​: 0 when all rows are one class, 0.5 for a 50/50 two-class node. A decision tree uses it, like entropy, to pick the split whose children are purest.Note ML-091Entropy, information gain and Gini
G-848Global minimumThe lowest point of the whole function.Note ML-056Gradient descent
G-849Global poolingPooling that uses the whole feature map as one window, giving one number per map (its max or its average). It can replace the Flatten layer and needs far fewer parameters in the next layer, which reduces overfitting.Note DL-044Pooling
G-850Glorot (Xavier) and He initialisationWays to choose the spread of random starting weights from the layer sizes.Note DL-018Xavier and He initialisation
G-851GloVeWord vectors learned from how often words appear near each other: training makes the dot product of two words’ vectors match the log of their co-occurrence probability (Pennington et al. 2014).Note DL-072Word embeddings
G-852Good fitCapturing the pattern while ignoring the noise.Note ML-007Overfitting
G-853Goodness-of-fit testA check of whether the counts in one categorical column match the shares we claimed (a chi-square test against claimed proportions); df=k−1 for k categories.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-854Google ColabGoogle’s browser-based Jupyter notebooks, saved in Google Drive.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-855GPTA language model that writes text by predicting the next token again and again (Generative Pre-trained Transformer); it is built from transformer decoder blocks only.Note DL-087Decoder-only GPT
G-856GPUA graphics chip that runs deep learning maths much faster than a CPU.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-857Gradient gi​How fast row i‘s loss changes as the previous prediction for that row moves (the first derivative of its loss with respect to that prediction). XGBoost uses it with the Hessian hi​ in a second-order approximation of the loss to build the next tree.Note ML-120Gradient boosting
G-863Gradient (of the loss)How fast the loss changes with each weight and bias, collected in one vector (the partial derivatives of the loss); it points in the direction in which the loss rises fastest.Note DL-015Backpropagation
G-858Gradient as a row vectorWriting the gradient as one row of partial derivatives, ∇f=[∂f/∂x1​,…,∂f/∂xn​]∈R1×n; this convention makes the chain rule a matrix product.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-859Gradient boostingA way to build a model from many trees added one by one: it starts from a simple guess, and each new tree is trained on the mistakes (pseudo-residuals) of the ensemble so far (a boosting algorithm).Note ML-114Gradient boosting
G-860Gradient checkingChecking that a gradient formula is right by comparing it with a numerical estimate made by nudging each weight a tiny amount (finite differences), measured by the relative error.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-861Gradient clippingCapping the gradient before each update: if its overall size (its norm) is above a chosen limit, it is scaled down to that limit with its direction kept, so exploding gradients cannot make huge weight jumps.Note DL-018Exploding gradient and gradient clipping
G-862Gradient descentFinding the lowest point of a function by repeated small steps downhill.Note ML-056Gradient descent
G-864Gradient routingIn max pooling’s backward pass, sending each gradient only to the position of its window’s maximum.Note DL-048Backpropagation in a CNN
G-866Grand meanThe mean of all values from all groups pooled together; ANOVA measures how far the values and the group means lie from it to split the total variation.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-867Grand totalThe sum of every cell of a contingency table: the size of the whole sample.Note MA-013Venn diagrams and contingency tables
G-868GraphvizThe graph-drawing program (dot) that lays out tree diagrams for dtreeviz and export_graphviz.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-869GRE, TOEFLExams taken by students applying to graduate programmes abroad; the first two inputs of the admission data.Note DL-013ANN for regression
G-870Greedy decodingPredicting by choosing the most likely token at each step and feeding it back.Note DL-068Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-871Greedy searchTaking the best split at each node without looking ahead.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-872Grid searchTraining a model for every combination of listed settings and keeping the best by cross-validation.Note ML-037Grid and random search
G-873Grid-like topologyData arranged on a regular grid, such as a time series (1D, one value per time step) or an image (2D, rows and columns of pixels); the kind of data CNNs are built to process.Note DL-040Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-874Grouping effectElastic Net’s tendency to give correlated inputs similar coefficients instead of keeping only one.Note ML-068Elastic Net
G-875handle_unknownOneHotEncoder parameter that decides what happens to categories never seen in training.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-876handle_unknown=“ignore”OneHotEncoder setting that outputs all zeros for a category not seen in training.Note ML-028One-hot encoding
G-877Hard assignmentGiving each observation wholly to one cluster (responsibility 0 or 1).Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-878Hard votingPredicting the label that most base models predict.Note ML-097Voting ensembles
G-879Hard-margin SVMThe SVM that allows no point inside the margin or on the wrong side; it needs perfectly separable data.Note ML-087Support vector machines
G-880Harmonic meanAn average that stays close to the smaller of the values, so one low value pulls it down; F1 uses it to combine precision and recall. For two values: 2ab/(a+b).Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-881He normalA way to set starting weights for ReLU layers: draw them from a normal distribution with standard deviation 2/fan-in​, so the signal keeps roughly the same size from layer to layer.Note DL-030Xavier and He initialisation
G-882He uniformA way to set starting weights for ReLU layers: draw them evenly between −6/fan-in​ and +6/fan-in​, so the signal keeps roughly the same size from layer to layer.Note DL-030Xavier and He initialisation
G-883HeadOne of several attention units that run side by side in a multi-head attention layer, each a complete self-attention with its own learned WQ​, WK​, WV​; each head gives its own table of attention weights, its own point of view.Note DL-078Multi-head attention
G-884Header (of a file)The line of a file that holds the column names.Note ML-014CSV files
G-885Headers (HTTP)Extra information sent with a request, such as the User-Agent.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-886HeatmapA table drawn as coloured cells, darker for larger values.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-887Hessian hi​How fast row i‘s gradient changes as the previous prediction moves (the second derivative of that row’s loss with respect to the prediction). XGBoost uses it together with the gradient to compute leaf weights and split gains.Note ML-120XGBoost
G-888Hessian matrixThe table of how a many-input function’s slopes change, which measures its curvature: the symmetric n×n matrix of all second partial derivatives of f:Rn→R.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-889HeteroscedasticityPrediction errors (residuals) whose spread changes with the predicted value, often widening like a funnel; it breaks the equal-spread assumption (homoscedasticity) of linear regression.Note ML-055Assumptions of linear regression
G-890Hidden layerA layer of neurons between the input and output layers; it works on the output of the layer before and passes what it finds on, so the network can build up more complex patterns.Note DL-002Neural networks
G-891Hidden state (ht​)The RNN’s running summary of the inputs so far: the recurrent layer’s output at time step t.Note DL-056Recurrent neural network (RNN)
G-892hidden_layer_sizesMLPClassifier setting: the number of nodes in each hidden layer, e.g. (4, 4).Note DL-009Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-893Hierarchical clusteringClustering that builds a hierarchy of clusters, from single points up to one cluster.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-894Hierarchical representationFeatures built in levels: simple ones in lower layers, more abstract ones in higher layers.Note DL-065Deep (stacked) RNNs
G-895High bias, low variance algorithmAn algorithm too simple to fit the training data well but stable across samples, such as linear regression; it underfits.Note ML-099Bagging
G-896High cardinalityA categorical column with very many different categories.Note ML-021Pandas Profiling
G-897High-dimensional dataData with a very large number of columns.Note ML-045Curse of dimensionality
G-898Hinge lossThe SVM’s error for one point: 0 when the point is on the correct side and outside the margin, growing in a straight line the further it goes past the margin; formula max(0,1−y(wTx+b)).Note ML-088Hinge loss and soft margin
G-899HistogramA bar chart of how many values fall in each equal range (bin) of a numerical column.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-900History objectThe object Keras’ fit returns: its .history holds the loss and metrics of every epoch, used to draw the training curves.Note DL-011Training curves (History)
G-901Hold-out setRows set aside before training, used only to produce honest predictions or scores.Note ML-121Stacking and blending
G-902HomoscedasticityPrediction errors (residuals) with the same spread for every predicted value; an assumption of linear regression, checked by plotting residuals against predictions.Note ML-055Assumptions of linear regression
G-903Horizontal flipMirroring an image left to right; a data augmentation step that gives the model new training images of the same class.Note DL-050Data augmentation
G-904HTMLThe language web pages are written in: a tree of nested tags.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-905Huber lossA regression loss that is half the squared error for errors up to δ and grows in a straight line beyond; it acts like MSE for small errors and like MAE for large ones, so outliers pull less.Note DL-014Huber loss
G-906Hue, style, sizePlot settings that show an extra column by colour, marker shape or dot size.Note MA-007Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-907Hyper-cuboidA box in many dimensions: the region a tree’s cuts carve out.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-910HyperparameterA setting of an algorithm chosen before training, such as a tree’s max_depth.Note ML-028Hyperparameter tuning
G-908Hyperparameter importanceHow much each hyperparameter affected the score in a study; the values add up to 1.Note ML-128Optuna
G-909Hyperparameter tuningTrying several hyperparameter values and keeping the best.Note ML-028Hyperparameter tuning
G-911HyperplaneA flat surface in more than three dimensions; the model for three or more input columns.Note ML-052Equation of a hyperplane
G-2214Hypothesis (Bayes’ theorem)The statement whose probability we want, such as “Steve is a librarian” or “the email is spam”.Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-912Hypothesis functionA model written as a function h(x) that maps an input to a prediction.Note ML-109AdaBoost
G-913Hypothesis testingChecking a claim about a population parameter with a sample.Note MA-038Hypothesis testing: null and alternative
G-914Identity initialisationStarting the recurrent weight matrix Wh​ as the identity matrix (1 on the diagonal, 0 elsewhere), so at the start of training multiplying by it leaves the gradient unchanged instead of shrinking it.Note DL-060Long-term dependency problem
G-915Identity matrixThe matrix that leaves every vector unchanged.Note ML-047Linear transformations and matrices
G-916If-else ladderA long chain of hand-written if conditions, one per case; the traditional way to code rules, which breaks down when the cases are too many or keep changing.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-917ILSVRCThe ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge: 1,000 classes, about 1.2 million training photos.Note DL-051Pretrained models and ImageNet
G-918Image captioningProducing a sentence that describes an image.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-919Image classificationDeciding what a picture contains, e.g. dog or not dog.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-2268Image segmentationDividing an image into regions by saying which pixels belong to which object.Note DL-044Pooling
G-920ImageNetA very large labelled image dataset with a yearly classification competition.Note DL-003History of deep learning
G-921Imbalanced dataData in which one class is much rarer than another.Note ML-009Imbalanced data
G-922imbalanced-learnA Python library (imblearn) of tools that rebalance the classes by adding or removing rows (resampling techniques), plus balanced ensembles, with a fit_resample method.Note ML-127Random under- and oversampling
G-923IMDB dataset50,000 film reviews labelled positive or negative, a standard sentiment-analysis dataset.Note DL-057Recurrent neural network (RNN)
G-924Immediate derivativeThe part of a derivative that comes only from a weight’s direct use at step t: the derivative of ht​ with respect to the weight with ht−1​ held fixed.Note DL-059Backpropagation through time (BPTT)
G-925Importance Ii​The weight of feature i in the toy model’s loss.Note DL-090Superposition and nearly perpendicular directions
G-926Impossible eventAn event that contains no outcome, so it can never happen, such as rolling a 7 with one die; it is the empty set ∅ and has probability 0.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-927ImputationFilling in missing values, for example with the mean, median or mode.Note ML-022Missing values
G-928Inactive constraintAn inequality constraint that the unconstrained minimum already satisfies, so it plays no part in the answer; its Lagrange multiplier is 0.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-929include_biasPolynomialFeatures setting that adds a column of 1s (the power 0), which acts as an intercept; LinearRegression fits its own intercept anyway, so either setting works.Note ML-060Polynomial features
G-930Increasing functionA function whose output grows whenever its input grows, such as the log; it keeps the position of a maximum.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-931Incremental learning (incremental training)Training on small pieces of data over time, keeping what was learned before (the opposite of batch learning).Note ML-004Online learning
G-933Independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.)Values that do not affect each other and all come from the same distribution.Note MA-033Central limit theorem
G-934Independent eventsEvents where one happening does not change the probability of the other.Note MA-016Independent and mutually exclusive events
G-935Independent modelsModels whose mistakes are unrelated, so one being wrong says nothing about the others.Note ML-096Voting ensembles
G-936Independent two-sample t-testA t-test comparing the means of two separate, non-overlapping groups.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-937Independent variablesAnother name for the features: the input columns X that a model uses to predict the output.Note ML-012Supervised learning
G-938IndexThe labels down the left side of a DataFrame, one per row (0, 1, 2, … by default); pandas uses them to name and select rows.Note ML-014CSV files
G-2278Indicator 1[…]A sign that gives 1 when the condition in the brackets holds and 0 otherwise, so it can switch terms on and off inside a formula (for example the ReLU mask).Note DL-048Backpropagation in a CNN
G-2279Self-supervised learningLearning where the labels are made from the data itself, such as the next word of a text; it lets a model learn from any amount of unlabelled data, with no human labelling.Note DL-067Large language models (LLMs)
G-939Inertia (of an organisation)A big organisation’s resistance to changing direction once it has started.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-940inertia_The number stored on a trained KMeans model that measures how tight its clusters are: the total squared distance from each point to its cluster’s centroid (its WCSS). The elbow method plots it against k.Note ML-123Elbow method and WCSS
G-943Inference (statistics)A conclusion about a population drawn from a sample.Note MA-004Inferential statistics
G-941Inference (vs prediction)Learning how the inputs affect the output, rather than only predicting it; not the deployment sense (running a trained model) nor inferential statistics.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-942Inference engineThe part of an expert system that applies the rules to answer a question.Note ML-002Symbolic AI and expert systems
G-944Inferential statisticsStatistics that draws conclusions about a population from a sample.Note MA-004Inferential statistics
G-945Inflection pointA point where a curve switches between bending down and bending up; for the normal curve, at μ±σ.Note MA-024Normal distribution
G-946Information gainHow much a split reduces the mix of labels: the parent’s entropy minus the weighted entropy of its children; the tree splits on the highest.Note ML-091Entropy, information gain and Gini
G-947InitialisationGiving every weight and bias its starting value before training begins; a bad start can cause vanishing or exploding gradients or slow convergence.Note DL-029Weight initialisation
G-948Input / outputThe columns we know / the column we want to predict.Note ML-003Supervised learning
G-949Input feedingJoining the previous step’s attention output h~i−1​ to the next decoder input, so the model remembers its past alignment choices; an option in Luong’s attention.Note DL-070Luong (multiplicative) attention
G-950Input gate (it​)The LSTM gate that adds new important information to the cell state: a sigmoid layer whose outputs, between 0 and 1, scale the candidate values before they are added.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-952Input layerThe first layer of a neural network, with one node per input column; it takes in the data and passes the values on without calculating anything.Note DL-002Neural networks
G-953InspectBrowser tool that shows which tag draws each part of a page.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-954Instance set Ij​The rows that land in leaf j.Note ML-120Gradient boosting
G-955Instance-based learningLearning by storing the training data and comparing new points with it.Note ML-006Instance-based learning
G-956Integer encodingReplacing each word by its index (a whole number) in the vocabulary, so a network such as an RNN can read text as numbers.Note DL-057Tokenization and integer encoding of text
G-957IntegrationFinding the area under a curve by adding up infinitely many thin strips.Note MA-022Probability density function (PDF)
G-958Inter-sequence attentionAttention between two different sequences, such as an output and an input sentence.Note DL-077Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-959Interaction termA product of two inputs, such as xy, that lets one input’s effect depend on another.Note ML-060Polynomial regression
G-960InterceptThe line’s value when the input is 0; b in y=mx+b.Note ML-049Best-fit line and squared error
G-961intercept_The attribute of a fitted scikit-learn linear model that holds the learned intercept b, the prediction when every input is 0.Note ML-049Simple linear regression
G-962InterferenceThe part of a feature’s reading that comes from other active features, in proportion to the cosines between their directions.Note DL-090Superposition and nearly perpendicular directions
G-963Internal covariate shiftThe way the values a layer receives keep changing their spread and centre during training, because the layers before it keep updating (the change in the distribution of a network’s activations).Note DL-031Covariate shift
G-964InterpolationPlacing a new point on the segment between two existing points.Note ML-127SMOTE
G-965InterpretabilityHow well people can understand why a model makes its decisions.Note ML-108Feature importance
G-966Interquartile range (IQR)The width of the middle half of the data: Q3 - Q1.Note ML-019Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-967Intersection (A ∩ B)The set of elements that are in both A and B, such as the points inside both of two half-planes; for events, the event that both A and B happen.Note MA-015Events and sample spaces
G-968Inverse matrixThe matrix that undoes another: their product is the identity matrix.Note ML-053Normal equation
G-969Inverse square root decayLowering the learning rate in proportion to 1/step​ after the warm-up, so the steps get smaller and the weights can settle near a minimum; the transformer paper’s schedule.Note DL-086Learning-rate warm-up schedule
G-970Inverted dropoutDropout that scales the kept outputs up by 1/(1−p) during training, so prediction needs no change; what Keras does.Note DL-024Dropout
G-971IoT sensorA device that measures something and sends the readings over the internet.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-972IQR method (IQR rule, IQR proximity rule)Outlier detection that flags values beyond 1.5 IQR outside the box (Q1​ to Q3​); for skewed columns.Note ML-019IQR outlier method
G-973Iris dataset150 iris flowers of three species, with four measurements each; a classic classification dataset.Note MA-027Central limit theorem
G-974isnullThe pandas method that marks each missing cell True.Note ML-034Missing values
G-975ISO weekThe week number of the ISO calendar, from .dt.isocalendar().week; week 1 holds the year’s first Thursday.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-976Iteration (MICE)One pass that re-predicts the gaps of every column once, in order.Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-977Iteration 0The starting table, with every gap filled by its column mean.Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-978Iterative imputerFilling missing values by predicting each column from the other columns, over and over (multivariate imputation); its algorithm is MICE.Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-980JacobianThe table (matrix) of all first partial derivatives of a function with several inputs and outputs, one row per output and one column per input, Jij​=∂fi​/∂xj​; it shows how every output changes with every input near a point.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-979Jacobian determinantThe factor by which a function stretches or shrinks small areas or volumes near a point: the determinant of its Jacobian, detJ.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-982Jensen’s inequalityFor a convex function, the function of a weighted average is at most the weighted average of the function.Note MA-067Convex sets and convex optimisation
G-981Jensen’s inequality (for the log)The log of a weighted average is at least the weighted average of the logs.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-983joblibA library that saves and loads Python objects like pickle, better suited to large arrays.Note ML-028Saving models with pickle
G-984Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemmaA cloud of n points in many dimensions can be copied into far fewer dimensions, about logn/ε2, with every squared distance kept within a factor 1±ε.Note DL-090Superposition and nearly perpendicular directions
G-986Joint probabilityThe probability that two events happen together, P(A∩B).Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-985Joint probability distributionThe joint probabilities of every combination of values of two variables; they sum to 1.Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-987JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)A plain-text format for structured data, made of objects and arrays, that almost every language can read; used by APIs.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-988JSON LinesA JSON file with one object per line, read with lines=True.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-989JSON viewerA tool that lays out JSON text as a tree to show its structure.Note ML-016APIs
G-990JupyterTool for notebooks that mix code, output and text.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-991JupyterLabThe program that runs Jupyter notebooks in a web browser.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-993k (k-means)The number of clusters k-means makes; chosen by us.Note ML-122K-means
G-992k (n_neighbors)The number of neighbours that vote; KNN’s main hyperparameter.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-994k-distance plotA plot of every point’s distance to its k-th nearest point, sorted from small to large; the bend where it shoots up gives a good eps for DBSCAN.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-996k-meansA clustering algorithm that repeatedly assigns points to the nearest centre and moves each centre to the mean of its points.Note ML-122K-means
G-995k-means binningBinning whose edges lie halfway between the centres of the groups found by k-means.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-997k-means++The default way KMeans picks its starting centroids: one by one, with far-away points more likely to be picked.Note ML-123K-means
G-998K-nearest neighbours (KNN)Predicting from the answers of the k closest stored points.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-999KaggleA website for sharing datasets and notebooks and for ML competitions.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1000KBinsDiscretizerscikit-learn’s class for equal width, equal frequency and k-means binning.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-1003KerasThe high-level interface built into TensorFlow for defining and training networks.Note DL-011Keras workflow
G-1001Keras TunerA Python library (keras_tuner) that searches for good hyperparameters of a Keras model.Note DL-039Keras Tuner
G-1002Keras workflowBuild, compile, fit, predict: the four steps of every Keras model.Note DL-011Keras workflow
G-1009Kernel (Jupyter)The running Python process behind a notebook.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-2273Kernel (KDE)A small symmetric bump with area 1, placed on each point to build a KDE curve.Note ML-019Kernel density estimation (KDE)
G-2274Kernel (Keras)Keras’ name for a layer’s weight matrix.Note DL-026L1 and L2 regularisation in neural networks
G-1004Kernel (SVM)A function of two points, K(a,b), that returns their dot product in the higher-dimensional space, ϕ(a)⋅ϕ(b), directly from the original values (not the Jupyter kernel).Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1005Kernel density estimate (KDE)A smooth curve that estimates a column’s PDF from its values, built by adding a kernel centred on every data point; a KDE plot draws it.Note ML-019Kernel density estimation (KDE)
G-1006Kernel function K(a,b)A function of two points that returns the dot product they would have after lifting to a higher-dimensional space, ϕ(a)⋅ϕ(b), computed straight from the original points, so the lifted features are never built.Note ML-090Kernel trick
G-1007Kernel transformationA loose name for lifting the data to the higher-dimensional space with the feature map ϕ.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1008Kernel trickMaking non-linear data separable by mapping it to a higher dimension, without building the new columns.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1011KeyIn attention, the vector each word offers to be compared with a query; the dot product of the query with a key scores how much attention that word gets.Note DL-074Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-1010Key and valueIn attention, the vectors of the words being looked at: keys are compared with the query to get the weights, and values are mixed with those weights; in cross-attention both come from the encoder’s input words.Note DL-074Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-1012Key, value (in an MLP)Geva et al.’s names for a row of the first matrix (a pattern detector) and the matching direction of the second matrix (what gets written).Note DL-089MLP blocks as fact storage
G-1013KKT conditionsThe four checks a point must pass to be a minimum when some constraints are inequalities: the Lagrangian’s gradient is zero (stationarity), the point obeys every constraint (primal feasibility), every multiplier is at least 0 (dual feasibility), and each multiplier is 0 unless its constraint is tight (complementary slackness).Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-1014KL divergence, focal loss, triplet lossLosses for autoencoders, object detection and embeddings, taught with those networks.Note DL-014Loss functions in deep learning
G-1015KMeansscikit-learn’s k-means class, in sklearn.cluster.Note ML-123K-means
G-1016KNeighborsClassifierscikit-learn’s KNN classifier; n_neighbors=5 by default.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-1017KNN imputerFilling a missing value from the most similar rows (multivariate imputation, KNNImputer).Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-1018Knowledge baseThe collection of rules inside an expert system.Note ML-002Symbolic AI and expert systems
G-1019Kruskal-Wallis testA test of whether several groups differ that works on the ranks of the values, so it does not assume normality; an alternative to one-way ANOVA.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-1021KurtosisHow heavy the tails of a distribution are compared with a normal curve; the fourth moment.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-1020Kurtosis riskIn finance, the risk of extreme gains or losses from fat-tailed returns.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-1022KV cacheStoring the key and value vectors of earlier positions so that each new step computes them only for the new word.Note DL-085Transformer inference (autoregressive decoding, KV cache, beam search)
G-1023L-BFGSAn optimiser that uses the curvature of the loss without storing the full Hessian: it builds a stand-in for it from only the last few steps and gradient changes, saving memory (limited-memory BFGS, a quasi-Newton method). scikit-learn’s default logistic regression solver.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1024L1 lossAnother name for the mean absolute error used as a training loss.Note DL-014Loss functions in deep learning
G-1025L1 normThe sum of the absolute values of the components.Note MA-049Vector magnitude, distance and scalar operations
G-1026L1 regularisationAnother name for the absolute-value penalty used by Lasso.Note ML-066Lasso regression
G-1027l1_ratioThe share of the total penalty given to the L1 (Lasso) part.Note ML-068Elastic Net
G-1028L2 norm (norm, magnitude, length of a vector)The usual magnitude of a vector, its distance from the origin: the square root of the sum of squared components, ∥w∥=w12​+w22​+…​.Note MA-049Vector magnitude, distance and scalar operations
G-1029L2 regularisationAnother name for the squared-coefficient penalty used by Ridge.Note ML-062Ridge regression
G-1032LabelThe answer an example comes with, the value a model learns to predict, such as the digit an image shows; another name for the target or output.Note ML-003Supervised learning
G-1030Label encodingReplacing the classes of the target by 0, 1, 2, …; for the output column only.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-2172Label propagationSemi-supervised method in which labels hop from labelled observations to their nearest neighbours, step by step.Note ML-003Semi-supervised learning
G-1031Label smoothingReplacing the one-hot target by a slightly softer one, (1−ε) on the correct word plus ε/K on every word, so training stops pushing the model towards complete certainty.Note DL-086Label smoothing
G-1033LabelEncoderscikit-learn’s class for label encoding the target.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-1034Labelled dataData that includes the output column.Note ML-003Supervised learning
G-1035labels_The cluster number of every training row, after fitting.Note ML-123K-means
G-1036Lagrange multiplierA number attached to one constraint; at the answer it scales the constraint’s gradient to match the objective’s, and measures how much the constraint costs.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-1037LagrangianOne function that packs an objective and its constraints together: the objective plus each constraint times its multiplier, f+∑i​λi​gi​; setting its gradient to zero gives the conditions for the constrained minimum.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-1039Lambda (λ, reg_lambda)XGBoost’s setting that holds its trees back (regularisation): it is added to the number of residuals in the denominators of the similarity score and leaf output, which shrinks scores, gains and outputs, most for leaves with few residuals; default 1.Note ML-118XGBoost
G-1038Lambda (λ, power transform)The power used by a power transform, learned separately for each column.Note ML-030Power transformer
G-1040Lambda (Python)A one-line Python function without a name, such as lambda x: x**2.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1041lambdas_The PowerTransformer attribute holding the learned λ of each column.Note ML-030Power transformer
G-1042Language modellingTraining a model to predict the next word of a text.Note DL-067Large language models (LLMs)
G-1043Laplace approximationReplacing a distribution near its peak with a normal distribution whose width comes from the curvature there (the Hessian).Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1044Laplace distributionA peaked, heavy-tailed distribution with density e−∣x−μ∣/b/(2b).Note MA-072MAP estimation
G-1045Laplace smoothingAdding a small count (usually 1) to every count so that no probability is 0.Note ML-083Naive Bayes
G-1046Large language model (LLM)A transformer language model with billions of parameters, trained on a vast amount of text.Note DL-067Large language models (LLMs)
G-1047Lasso regressionLinear regression with a penalty on the sum of absolute coefficients (L1); it shrinks coefficients and can set some exactly to 0, which removes those features.Note ML-066Lasso regression
G-1048LatencyThe delay between a request and its answer; high for KNN on large data.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-1049Latent semantic analysis (LSA)Describing each document by a few topic directions of the document-word matrix (its top k singular directions, found with the SVD), so that texts on one topic line up.Note MA-060Latent semantic analysis
G-1050Latent variableA variable in a model that is never observed, such as the component that produced a point.Note MA-073Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
G-1051Lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN)A region of the thalamus that passes visual signals on to V1.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1052Law of large numbersThe more trials, the closer a share of trials gets to the true probability.Note MA-021Probability mass function (PMF)
G-1053Law of total probabilityThe rule for the overall probability of an event: add its probability under each case, weighted by how likely that case is, P(B)=∑i​P(B∣Ai​)P(Ai​), when the cases Ai​ are mutually exclusive and cover every possibility.Note MA-019Bayes’ theorem
G-1056LayerA group of neurons in a neural network that all work on the output of the layer before; stacking layers lets the network find more complex patterns.Note ML-002Neural networks
G-1054Layer normalisationPutting each observation’s numbers on one scale by itself, without depending on the batch: subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation across its own features, then scale and shift each feature by learned γj​ and βj​.Note DL-080Layer normalisation
G-1055Layer numberThe position of a layer, from 0 for the input layer to the output layer.Note DL-008MLP notation and parameter count
G-1057Lazy learningAnother name for instance-based learning: no work until a question arrives.Note ML-006Instance-based learning
G-1058lbfgsThe default solver of LogisticRegression; supports L2 or no penalty.Note ML-080Logistic regression
G-1059LDALinear discriminant analysis: a way to build new columns that uses the class labels (a supervised method), along the directions that best separate the classes.Note ML-022Feature extraction
G-1060Leaf nodeA node that is not split; it gives the prediction.Note ML-091Decision trees
G-1061Leaf value (γjm​)The constant a leaf adds to the model, chosen to minimise the loss of the rows in that leaf.Note ML-115Gradient boosting
G-1062Leaf value in log-oddsThe amount a leaf adds to the log-odds in gradient boosting for classification, converted from the leaf’s residuals because a probability cannot be added to log-odds: ∑r/∑p(1−p) over the leaf’s rows.Note ML-116Gradient boosting
G-1063Leaf weight wj​The output value of leaf j of a tree: the number the tree gives every observation that lands in that leaf; XGBoost solves for these values.Note ML-120XGBoost
G-1064Leaky ReLUA ReLU variant with a small slope for negative inputs, so nodes do not die.Note DL-028Leaky ReLU, PReLU, ELU and SELU
G-1065Learnable (trainable) parametersThe weights and biases that training changes; for a convolution layer, the filter values and one bias per filter.Note DL-046CNN architecture (LeNet-5)
G-1066Learned positional embeddingA trainable vector per position, learned like a word embedding.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-1073LearningFinding rules (patterns) from examples.Note ML-002Machine learning
G-2163Learning pathWhich Notes to read before which.Course map
G-1068Learning rate (η)How strongly each update changes the model; in gradient descent, the number the slope is multiplied by to get the step size.Note ML-005Learning rate
G-1067Learning rate (η) in gradient boostingThe fraction of each tree’s output that is added to the model, the same for every tree; typically 0.1.Note ML-114Gradient boosting
G-1069Learning rate (AdaBoost)A number that scales how much each weak learner’s vote (its alpha) counts in AdaBoost; values below 1 slow learning.Note ML-112AdaBoost
G-1070Learning rate scheduler (learning schedule)A rule that changes the learning rate as training goes on, usually lowering it.Note DL-021Improving a neural network
G-1071Learning rate warm-upStarting training with a very small learning rate and raising it over the first epochs or steps (4,000 steps in the transformer paper).Note DL-021Learning-rate warm-up schedule
G-1076Least-squares lossThe total squared gap between the targets and a model’s predictions, ∥y−Φθ∥2; fitting picks the parameters θ that make it smallest. Its gradient is −2(y−Φθ)TΦ.Note MA-063Ordinary least squares (closed form)
G-1077LeCun initialisationA way to pick a network’s random starting weights: draw them from a normal distribution with standard deviation 1/fan-in​ (fan-in is the number of inputs to a node), so the signal keeps a steady spread from layer to layer; the start SELU needs (Keras lecun_normal).Note DL-030Xavier and He initialisation
G-1078Left null spaceThe set of output vectors perpendicular to every column of a matrix, so the matrix can never produce them; in the SVD it is spanned by the left singular vectors ur+1​,…,um​.Note MA-058Singular value decomposition
G-1079Left singular vector (ui​)One of the output directions of the SVD: the unit vector that a right singular vector lands on, stretched by its singular value (Avi​=σi​ui​); the columns of U.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1080LeNet-5An early network for reading handwritten digits, built by LeCun et al. in 1998 (a CNN): two blocks of convolution then pooling (conv-pool blocks), then layers of 120, 84 and 10 nodes.Note DL-045CNN architecture (LeNet-5)
G-1081LeptokurticSaid of a distribution whose tails are fatter than the normal’s (excess kurtosis above 0), so extreme values and outliers are more common.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-1082Levene’s testA check of whether two or more groups have the same spread (a hypothesis test for equal variances, H0​: they do). Used before a two-sample t-test to choose between the equal-variance test and Welch’s t-test.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1083LiDARA sensor that measures distances to nearby objects with laser light.Note DL-003History of deep learning
G-1084LightGBMMicrosoft’s gradient boosting library, aimed at speed and low memory use.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-1086LikelihoodHow probable the observed data is under given parameter values; read as a function of the parameters with the data fixed.Note MA-069Likelihood
G-1085Likelihood function L(θ∣data)The likelihood as a function of the parameters, with the data held fixed: the product of the densities (or probabilities) of all observations.Note MA-069Likelihood
G-1087LimitThe value an expression approaches as a quantity (such as h) gets arbitrarily close to a target (such as 0).Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1088Line plotA scatter plot with the dots joined in order, used when x is time.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-1089Linear activationAn activation that passes a node’s weighted sum through unchanged, f(z)=z. Used in the output layer for regression.Note DL-013Activation functions
G-1090Linear algebraThe branch of mathematics that studies linear equations, vectors and matrices; ML uses it to store data (tables, text, images) as vectors and matrices and to work on a whole dataset in one step.Note MA-048Linear algebra roadmap
G-1091Linear combinationA sum of vectors each multiplied by a number, a1​v1​+⋯+ak​vk​; changing the numbers reaches different vectors, and all the vectors it can reach form the span.Note MA-052Linear combinations, span and basis
G-1092Linear interpolationPlacing a percentile between two neighbouring sorted values, in proportion to its position; the pandas default.Note ML-043Percentile outlier method
G-1093Linear programA problem of making a linear function as small as possible when the allowed choices are limited by linear inequalities (linear constraints). It is a common kind of convex problem with its own fast solvers.Note MA-068Linear and quadratic programming
G-1094Linear regressionA model that predicts a number from the inputs by fitting the straight line (or, with several inputs, the plane) that runs closest to all the training points.Note ML-049Simple linear regression
G-1095Linear relationshipA relationship between two columns that follows a straight line.Note ML-055Assumptions of linear regression
G-1097Linear transformationA change of the whole plane by a matrix that keeps grid lines straight and evenly spaced, and the origin fixed; algebraically, L(v+w)=L(v)+L(w) and L(cv)=cL(v).Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-1096Linear transformation to the number lineA linear transformation that sends each vector to a single number, keeping evenly spaced dots evenly spaced; its matrix is one row (1×n), so applying it is the same as a dot product with that row.Note MA-055Dot product
G-1098Linear variants of ReLUReLU variants that replace ReLU’s flat zero on the negative side with a straight line of small slope (Leaky ReLU and PReLU), so a node with negative inputs still has a gradient and keeps learning.Note DL-028Leaky ReLU, PReLU, ELU and SELU
G-1099LinearisationReplacing a function near a point by its tangent line (its first-order Taylor polynomial).Note MA-061Taylor series
G-1100Linearity of expectationThe rule that the expected value of a sum is the sum of the expected values, with constants scaling and shifting it: E[aX+bY+c]=aE[X]+bE[Y]+c, for any random variables.Note MA-012Expected value and variance of a random variable
G-1101Linearly dependentSaid of a set of vectors in which at least one can be built from the others by scaling and adding (a linear combination), so it adds nothing to the span.Note MA-052Linear combinations, span and basis
G-1102Linearly independentSaid of a set of vectors in which none can be built from the others, so each one adds a new direction to the span.Note MA-052Linear combinations, span and basis
G-1103Linearly separableData whose classes a straight line, plane or hyperplane can split.Note ML-069Logistic regression
G-2166LinkA labelled arrow on the course map from one Concept to another that says how they relate, with one of five types: needs, is a kind of, fixes, compared with, used in.Course map
G-1104LinkageThe rule that measures the distance between two clusters, for example the distance between their closest points or their average distance; hierarchical clustering merges the two closest clusters by this rule, so the linkage shapes the result.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-1105List of gridsSeveral separate sets of hyperparameter values to try (parameter grids), passed to the search together, so values that do not work together never meet in one combination.Note ML-106Grid and random search
G-1106List, dictionaryPython’s ordered collection [...], and its key: value pairs {...}.Note ML-014CSV files
G-1107Load balancingSpreading requests across servers so all users are served quickly.Note ML-009Deployment
G-2204Loading (loading score)How much one original feature counts in a principal component (its weight there); it is one entry of that component’s eigenvector.Note ML-047PCA
G-1108Local linear mapThe linear transformation a smooth function behaves like near a point; its matrix is the Jacobian.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-1109Local maximumA point higher than everything near it but not the highest overall.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-1110Local minimumA point lower than everything around it, but not the lowest overall.Note ML-056Local minima and saddle points
G-1111Local optimum (k-means)A clustering where k-means has stopped but a better one exists, caused by a bad start.Note ML-124K-means
G-2250Locally linearSaid of a function that looks more and more like a linear transformation as we zoom in on any point.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-1112Log transformReplacing each value with its logarithm; pulls in a long right tail.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1113Log-likelihoodThe logarithm of the likelihood, which turns the product of probabilities into a sum of log probabilities; it peaks at the same parameters as the likelihood and is easier to compute and maximise.Note ML-072Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1114Log-log plotA plot with both axes on a log scale: it plots lny against lnx. On it a power law shows as a straight line.Note MA-030Pareto distribution and power laws
G-1115Log-normal distributionA distribution with a long tail to the right (right-skewed, continuous) whose values follow a normal distribution once you take their logarithm.Note MA-029Log-normal distribution
G-1116Log-oddsThe natural log of the odds, ln(p/(1−p)): it turns a probability between 0 and 1 into any number (0 at p=0.5), so a model such as logistic regression can predict it with a straight line, and the sigmoid turns it back into a probability.Note ML-116Gradient boosting
G-1117log1pNumPy’s function that adds 1 to each value and then takes the log, log(1+x), so the log transform also works when a value is 0.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1118Logical diagramA drawing of a neural network as a chain of data arrays (tensors) linked by the operations between them.Note DL-047Backpropagation in a CNN
G-1119Logistic functionAnother name for the sigmoid, 1/(1+e−z): the S-shaped function that squashes any number into a value between 0 and 1, read as a probability.Note ML-071Sigmoid function
G-1120Logistic regressionA classification algorithm that passes a weighted sum of the inputs through the sigmoid to give the probability of a class; the line (or plane) where that probability is 0.5 is the boundary it learns between the classes.Note ML-069Logistic regression
G-1122LogitThe raw score the final linear layer gives each vocabulary word, any number and not yet a probability; the softmax turns the logits into the probabilities of the next word.Note DL-084Unembedding, logits, temperature and sampling
G-1121Logit lensA way to see what a language model would predict partway through: after each block, pass its running vector (the residual stream) through the final LayerNorm and the unembedding to read which tokens it would predict if it stopped there. It shows the guess forming over the blocks.Note DL-088Logit lens
G-1123Long short-term memory (LSTM)A recurrent network (RNN) that carries two memories from one time step to the next, a long-term one (the cell state) and a short-term one (the hidden state), with gates that control what each memory keeps and passes on.Note DL-061LSTM (long short-term memory)
G-1124Long-term contextWhat matters for the sequence as a whole, kept from earlier steps.Note DL-061Long-term dependency problem
G-1126Long-term dependencyAn output that depends on an input many time steps earlier.Note DL-060Long-term dependency problem
G-1125Long-term dependency problemA simple RNN’s failure to link an output to an input many time steps earlier (a long-term dependency), because the gradient shrinks away as it flows back through time (the vanishing gradient through time).Note DL-060Long-term dependency problem
G-1127Look-ahead pointThe point that the momentum step alone would take the weights to, wt​−βvt−1​; Nesterov momentum measures the gradient there instead of at the current weights, so it corrects sooner and overshoots less.Note DL-035Nesterov accelerated gradient (NAG)
G-1128Lookup tableThe stored probabilities (class priors, and each feature value’s probability within each class) that Naive Bayes computes once in training and then looks up to score new rows.Note ML-083Naive Bayes
G-706Loss function (error function)A formula that measures how wrong a model’s predictions are; in deep learning, the error on one training row.Note ML-050Ordinary least squares (closed form)
G-1131Loss weightA number that scales one output’s loss in the total loss of a multi-output model.Note DL-054Keras functional API
G-1132Low bias, high variance algorithmAn algorithm that fits its training data very well but changes a lot with the data, such as a fully grown tree; it overfits.Note ML-099Bagging
G-1133Lower and upper limit (of a confidence interval)The two ends of a confidence interval: the point estimate minus and plus the margin of error, the range in which the parameter is estimated to lie.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-1134Lower bound B(θ;q)A simpler function that always sits at or below the log-likelihood and touches it when q are the current responsibilities. EM’s M-step climbs this bound, which pushes the log-likelihood up at least as much.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-1135LPALakh rupees per annum: a salary in hundreds of thousands of rupees per year.Note ML-049Simple linear regression
G-1137Luong attention (multiplicative, dot)Attention between a decoder state and the encoder states, scored by multiplying them: si⊤​hj​ (dot) or si⊤​Wa​hj​.Note DL-070Luong (multiplicative) attention
G-1139M-stepThe second step of each EM round (maximisation): with the responsibilities held fixed, re-estimate each component’s mean, covariance and weight as responsibility-weighted averages, so the fit to the data improves.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-1140Machine Learning (ML)Using statistics to let a machine find patterns (rules) in data by itself.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-1141Machine translationTranslating a sentence from one language into another.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1142Maclaurin seriesThe Taylor series around x0​=0: an infinite sum of powers of x, built from a function’s derivatives at 0, that approximates the function near 0.Note MA-061Taylor series
G-1143Macro averageThe plain mean of a metric (such as precision) over all classes, so every class counts equally however many rows it has.Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-1144Magnitude (of a quantity)The number part of a quantity, as opposed to its unit.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1145Majority classThe class with the most rows in imbalanced data.Note ML-127Imbalanced data
G-1146Majority votePredicting the class that most voters choose: the k neighbours in KNN, or the base models of an ensemble.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-1147make_blobsscikit-learn function that generates points around chosen centres.Note ML-123K-means
G-1149make_classificationscikit-learn function that creates random classification data.Note ML-070Logistic regression
G-1150make_column_transformerscikit-learn function that sets up different preprocessing for different columns (a column transformer) from (transformer, columns) pairs, without you naming the steps.Note ML-028Column transformer
G-1152make_pipelinescikit-learn function that chains steps such as preprocessing and a model into one object (a pipeline) from the objects alone, naming each step after its class.Note ML-028ML pipelines
G-1153make_regressionscikit-learn function that generates data following a linear pattern plus noise.Note ML-052Multiple linear regression
G-1154Many-to-many RNNAn RNN that takes a sequence and produces a sequence; also called sequence-to-sequence.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1155Many-to-one RNNAn RNN that reads a sequence and gives one output at the end.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1157MAP rulePredict the class that is most probable for the row, given its features (the class with the largest posterior probability; maximum a posteriori).Note ML-082Naive Bayes
G-1158MARMissing at random: the gaps depend on another, recorded column.Note ML-034Missing values
G-1159Margin (gap)The distance from a separating line to the nearest point of a class.Note ML-070Support vector machines
G-1160Margin (SVM)The full width of the empty band around an SVM’s separating line, from the nearest point of one class to the nearest point of the other (later shown to be 2/∥w∥); the SVM picks the line that makes this band widest.Note ML-086Support vector machines
G-1161Margin errorThe part of the soft-margin SVM loss, ∥w∥/2, that grows as the margin narrows; minimising it pushes the margin wider.Note ML-088Hinge loss and soft margin
G-1162Margin of errorThe distance from the point estimate to either end of a confidence interval.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-1163Margin-maximising hyperplaneThe flat boundary (hyperplane) that splits the classes while staying as far as possible from the nearest points of each (the largest margin); it is the decision boundary an SVM learns.Note ML-086Support vector machines
G-1164Marginal (simple, unconditional) probabilityThe probability of one variable’s value whatever the other variable does.Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-1165Marginal probability distributionAll the marginal probabilities of one variable, read from a joint table.Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-1166MarginalisingAdding up a table of probabilities of two variables (a joint distribution) over every value of one variable, which removes that variable and leaves the other’s probabilities.Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-1167MarginsThe row and column totals of a contingency table, where marginal probabilities are read.Note MA-014Joint and marginal probability
G-1168MarkdownA simple way to format text with symbols such as # and **.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1169Mask matrix MA matrix added to the attention scores: 0 where attention is allowed, −∞ where it is blocked.Note DL-082Masked self-attention
G-1170Masked language modelA pre-training task that hides some words and asks the model to predict them from both sides (BERT).Note DL-067Large language models (LLMs)
G-1171Masked multi-head attentionMulti-head attention with the causal mask in every head, so no word can take information from the words after it; the first sub-layer of the transformer decoder.Note DL-082Masked self-attention
G-1172Masked self-attentionSelf-attention in which each word can take information only from itself and earlier words: the later words’ scores get −∞ before the softmax, so their weights are 0, softmax(QKT/dk​​+M)V. It lets the decoder train on whole target sentences in one pass without seeing the future.Note DL-082Masked self-attention
G-1173Mathematical problemA business goal restated as a measurable target, such as a churn rate to reach.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-1174Mathematical transformationApplying one mathematical formula, such as the log or the square root, to every value of a column, usually to bring its distribution closer to normal.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1180MatrixA table of numbers in rows and columns (a 2D tensor); it can hold a dataset (one row per observation), and multiplying a vector by it transforms the vector.Note ML-010Tensors
G-1175Matrix (of a transformation)The grid of numbers that records a linear transformation: its columns are where the basis vectors land, which is enough to find where every vector lands.Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-1176Matrix calculusRules for differentiating expressions that contain vectors and matrices, such as a loss written in matrix form, so all the partial derivatives come out in one formula.Note ML-053Normal equation
G-1177Matrix factorisation (decomposition)Writing a matrix as a product of simpler matrices.Note MA-047Singular value decomposition
G-1178Matrix factorisation (recommenders)Predicting ratings as a viewer vector times a film vector, fitted on the known ratings only.Note MA-060Singular value decomposition
G-1179Matrix productThe single matrix BA that does the same as applying A and then B (their composition), so a chain of transformations can be done as one multiplication.Note MA-054Matrix multiplication as composition
G-1181Matrix-vector multiplicationMultiplying a matrix by a vector, Ax: each column of A is scaled by the matching entry of x and the results are added (a linear combination of the columns).Note MA-053Linear transformations and matrices
G-1182Max poolingPooling that keeps only the largest value in each window (usually 2 × 2), which shrinks the feature map while keeping the strongest response in each region.Note DL-044Pooling
G-1183Max-abs scalingDivide by the largest absolute value in the column, giving values from -1 to 1.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1184max_depthThe cap on a tree’s depth; None lets it grow until every leaf is pure.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1185max_featuresThe number of randomly chosen columns a tree considers at each split.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1186max_leaf_nodesThe cap on the number of leaves; the tree grows best-first until it is reached.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1187max_samplesThe number or share of rows each base model gets.Note ML-100Bagging
G-1188MaxAbsScalerscikit-learn’s class for max-abs scaling.Note ML-024Normalization
G-2217Maximal margin classifierThe classifier that separates the classes with the largest possible margin; the hard-margin SVM.Note ML-086Support vector machines
G-1189Maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimationChoosing the parameters with the largest posterior probability given the data, which weighs the likelihood by a prior belief about the parameters; in practice, minimise the negative log-likelihood minus the log prior.Note MA-072MAP estimation
G-1190Maximum likelihood estimate θ^ML​The parameter value where the likelihood function is highest.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1191Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)Fitting parameters by making the likelihood of the observed data as large as possible.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1192MCARMissing completely at random: the gaps have no relation to any value in the data.Note ML-034Missing values
G-1203MeanThe average of the values; the centre of the data.Note ML-018Measures of central tendency
G-1193Mean absolute deviationThe average absolute distance of the points from their mean. Sometimes also abbreviated MAD, which clashes with the median absolute deviation.Note MA-006Variance
G-1194Mean absolute error (MAE)The average absolute difference between actual and predicted values.Note ML-051Regression metrics
G-1195Mean centringSubtracting the mean from every value, so the column’s mean becomes 0.Note MA-049Vector magnitude, distance and scalar operations
G-1196Mean decrease in impurity (MDI)A score of how much a column helps the trees: its share of the total drop in impurity from all splits made on it, weighted and averaged over the trees (impurity-based feature importance, also called Gini importance).Note ML-108Feature importance
G-2237Mean difference (μd​)The average of each subject’s difference between its two measurements (a paired design); the paired t-test tests whether it is 0, μd​=0.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1197Mean imputationFilling every gap with the mean of the column’s known values.Note ML-035Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
G-1198Mean normalizationSubtract the mean and divide by the range, giving values from -1 to 1 centred on 0.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1199Mean of a random variableAnother name for its expected value: the probability-weighted average of its possible values, the average outcome over many repeats.Note MA-012Expected value and variance of a random variable
G-1200Mean square (MSB, MSW)A sum of squared distances divided by its degrees of freedom, which turns it into a variance (a measure of spread). ANOVA divides the between-group mean square (MSB) by the within-group one (MSW) to get the F statistic.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-1201Mean squared error (MSE)The average squared difference between actual and predicted values.Note ML-051Regression metrics
G-1204mean(axis=0)The mean of each column of an array.Note ML-124K-means
G-1205Measure of central tendencyA single number for the typical, central value of a column.Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-1206Measure of dispersionA number that describes how spread out a column is around its centre.Note MA-006Variance
G-1209MedianThe middle value of sorted data; the 50% percentile.Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-1207Median absolute deviation (MAD)The median distance of the values from their median.Note ML-021Outliers
G-1208Median imputationFilling every gap with the median of the column’s known values; better for skewed columns.Note ML-035Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
