G-1210MemoizationStoring the result of a function call and returning the stored result when the same input comes again.Note DL-019Memoization
G-1211meshgridNumPy function that builds every combination of x and y values: the grid for a decision surface.Note ML-085Decision surface and boundary
G-1212MesokurticSaid of a distribution whose tails are like the normal’s (excess kurtosis 0), so extreme values are about as common as under a normal distribution.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-1213Meta-modelThe final model in stacking: it takes the other models’ (base models’) predictions as its inputs and is trained to combine them.Note ML-095Stacking and blending
G-1214methodThe PowerTransformer setting that picks which formula reshapes the column: "box-cox" or "yeo-johnson".Note ML-030Power transformer
G-1215Metric (performance metric)A number that measures how well a model works, and so tells whether the work is moving in the right direction.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-1216MICEA way to fill gaps: each column’s missing values are predicted by a model trained on the other columns, and the rounds repeat until the filled values settle (Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations, the algorithm behind the iterative imputer).Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-1217Min-max scalingSubtract the column’s minimum and divide by its range, giving values from 0 to 1; the main normalization technique.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1218min_frequencyOneHotEncoder parameter that merges rare categories into one column.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-1219min_impurity_decreaseA tree setting: a split is made only if it makes the nodes purer by at least this much (the smallest weighted impurity decrease allowed).Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1220min_samples_leafThe smallest number of rows every leaf must keep.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1221min_samples_splitThe smallest number of rows a node must hold to be split.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1222Mini-batch gradient descentGradient descent that uses a small random group of rows for every update.Note ML-059Mini-batch gradient descent
G-1224MiniforgeA small installer with only conda and Python, using conda-forge.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1225Minimax inequalityTaking the smallest value over one argument and then the largest over the other never gives more than doing it in the other order: maxy​minx​φ≤minx​maxy​φ for any function of two arguments. It is why the dual problem’s answer is never above the primal’s (weak duality).Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-1226Minimum-norm solutionWhen many solutions fit equally well (the same least-squares error), the shortest one, with the smallest length (norm); what A+b returns.Note MA-060Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse
G-1227Minkowski distanceA family of distances between two points, (∑i​∣xi​−yi​∣p)1/p, set by the number p: p=2 gives the Euclidean distance and p=1 the Manhattan distance; KNN uses it to find the nearest neighbours.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-1228MinMaxScalerscikit-learn’s class for min-max scaling.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1229Minority classThe rare class in imbalanced data, usually the one we need to find.Note ML-127Imbalanced data
G-1230Minorizer / majorizerA simpler function that lies below (minorizer) or above (majorizer) the function being optimised (the objective) and touches it at the current point; maximising a minorizer (or minimising a majorizer) moves the objective the same way, which is how EM makes progress.Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-1231MinPts (min_samples)The DBSCAN setting for how many points a point’s eps-neighbourhood (the circle of radius eps around it) must hold for the region to count as dense, which makes the point a core point.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-1232Missing category imputationFilling every gap in a categorical column with a new category, “Missing”.Note ML-036Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
G-1233Missing indicatorA 0/1 (True/False) column recording whether a value was missing, added next to the imputed column so the model can learn whether being missing itself matters.Note ML-037Missing indicator
G-1234Missing valueAn empty entry, shown by pandas as NaN.Note ML-014Missing values
G-1236Mixed partial derivativeA second partial derivative taken with respect to two different variables, such as ∂2f/∂y∂x: how the slope along x changes as y changes; the off-diagonal entries of the Hessian.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1237Mixed variableA column holding both numerical and categorical data.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-1238Mixture weight πk​How big a share of a mixture one component k gets; the weights are non-negative and add up to 1.Note MA-073Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
G-1239ML algorithmA general method that finds the pattern between inputs and outputs in data.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-1240MLDLCMachine learning development life cycle: the guidelines for building an ML product from idea to product.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-1241MLE of a binomial pThe success probability of a binomial that makes the observed data most likely: the observed share of successes, p^​=x/n.Note MA-071Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1242MLE of a normal distributionThe normal curve that makes the data most likely: its mean is the sample mean and its variance the average squared distance from that mean (dividing by n), μ^​=xˉ and σ^2=∑(xi​−xˉ)2/n.Note MA-071Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1243MLE of an exponential rateThe rate of an exponential distribution that makes the observed waiting times most likely: one over their mean, λ^=n/∑xi​=1/xˉ.Note MA-071Exponential distribution
G-1244MLOpsRunning and maintaining ML models in production.Note ML-007MLOps and cost
G-1245MLP blockThe feed-forward part of a transformer block: it widens each token’s vector with a matrix (up-projection), applies an activation, shrinks it back (down-projection) and adds the result to the token’s vector.Note DL-089MLP blocks as fact storage
G-1246MLPClassifierscikit-learn’s class for a classifier built from layers of perceptrons (a multi-layer perceptron).Note DL-009Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-1247MM algorithmA way to optimise a hard function by repeatedly optimising a simpler one (a surrogate) that lies on one side of it and touches it at the current point; the name stands for minorize–maximize (or majorize–minimize).Note MA-074Expectation maximization (EM)
G-1248MNARMissing not at random: the gaps depend on the missing value itself.Note ML-034Missing values
G-1249MNISTA dataset of about 70,000 handwritten-digit images of 28 × 28 pixels.Note ML-022Feature extraction
G-1250ModalityA kind of data, such as text, images or audio.Note DL-071Transformer
G-1251ModeThe value that appears most often in the data, so it sits under the highest peak of a histogram or a distribution curve; it gives a centre for data that are not numbers, and a belief with several peaks has several modes.Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-1256ModelThe logic produced by training, used to give outputs for new inputs.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-1253Model drift / concept driftA model’s accuracy dropping as the real world changes; sometimes called model rot.Note ML-004Model drift
G-1254Model selectionTraining several algorithms and keeping the best.Note ML-009ML development life cycle
G-1257Model-based learningLearning a mathematical function from the data and predicting with it.Note ML-006Model-based learning
G-1258Momentum (optimizer)Gradient descent that keeps part of its past movement: each step follows an average of past gradients in which older ones count less and less (a velocity, an exponentially decaying average).Note DL-034SGD with momentum
G-1259monotonic_cstSetting that forces predictions to only rise or only fall as a column grows.Note ML-105Random forest
G-1260MonotonicityWhether a column’s values only go up, or only go down, from row to row.Note ML-021Pandas Profiling
G-1261Moore’s lawThe number of transistors on a chip doubles about every two years.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-1262Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse (A+)The closest thing to an inverse for a matrix that is not square or has no inverse (a generalised inverse): the SVD inverted with zero singular values left at zero, VΣ+UT.Note MA-060Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse
G-1263More extremeSaid of a possible test result with at least as much evidence against H0​ as the observed one, in the direction(s) H1​ points to; the p-value is the probability of a result this extreme or more extreme when H0​ is true.Note MA-041P-values
G-1264Most frequent value imputation (mode imputation)Filling every gap in a column with its mode.Note ML-036Simple imputation (mean, median, mode, constant)
G-2267Moving averageThe list of averages a sliding window gives: each output is the mean of the numbers under the window, so sharp jumps are smoothed out.Note DL-042Convolution operation and feature maps
G-1265Moving mean and moving varianceRunning averages of each node’s mean and variance over the training batches, kept during training (in batch normalization) and used in place of the batch’s own values at prediction.Note DL-031Batch normalisation
G-1266Multi-class classificationClassification where the output is one of more than two classes, such as the next word out of a whole vocabulary; the output layer has one node per class.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-1267Multi-class output layerAn output layer with one node per class; the highest output gives the prediction.Note DL-009Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-1268Multi-head attentionSeveral self-attentions (heads) run in parallel on the same input, each with its own weights so each can capture a different kind of relation between words; their outputs are joined and mixed by one more learned matrix, WO​.Note DL-078Multi-head attention
G-1269Multi-input modelA model that takes several inputs, such as a photo and a table.Note DL-054Keras functional API
G-1270Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)Many perceptrons organised in layers: input, hidden and output.Note DL-003Multi-layer perceptron (MLP)
G-1271Multi-layer stackingStacking with more than one layer of base models below the meta-model.Note ML-121Stacking and blending
G-1272Multi-output modelA model that predicts several targets at once, each from its own output layer.Note DL-054Keras functional API
G-1273MulticollinearityA relationship between input columns, so that one can be calculated (or largely predicted) from the others; it makes a linear model’s coefficients unstable and hard to interpret.Note ML-026Multicollinearity
G-1275MultimodalHaving more than one mode (two modes: bimodal).Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-1274Multimodal modelA model that takes in or produces more than one modality.Note DL-071Transformer
G-1276Multinomial logistic regressionLogistic regression extended to more than two classes: it gives each class a probability with the softmax. Also called softmax regression.Note ML-078Softmax regression
G-1277MultinomialNBNaive Bayes for count data, such as word counts.Note ML-084Naive Bayes
G-1278Multiple imputationMaking several filled copies of the data to see how unsure the fills are.Note ML-039Iterative imputation (MICE)
G-1279Multiple linear regressionLinear regression with several input columns.Note ML-052Multiple linear regression
G-2212Multiplication ruleThe chance that both A and B happen is the chance of B times the chance of A given B: P(A∩B)=P(A∣B)×P(B).Note MA-015Conditional probability
G-1280Multivariate analysisStudying more than two variables together.Note ML-019Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-1281Multivariate chain ruleHow to take a derivative when a function depends on its inputs through in-between (intermediate) variables: multiply the derivatives along each path and add the paths. In matrix form, a row gradient times a matrix of inner derivatives.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-1282Multivariate imputationFilling the gaps in one column using the values of the other columns too (as the KNN and iterative imputers do), so each fill fits the rest of its row.Note ML-034Missing values
G-1283Multivariate normal distributionThe bell-shaped (normal) distribution for several numbers at once, a vector; it is set by a mean vector (its centre) and a covariance matrix (its spread and how the numbers vary together).Note MA-073Multivariate normal distribution
G-1284Multivariate Taylor polynomialAn approximation of a function of several variables near a point, built from its derivatives there up to order n (the multivariate Taylor series cut after the k=n term); the second-order one uses the gradient and the Hessian.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1285Multivariate Taylor seriesAn approximation of a function of several variables near a point x0​ from all its derivatives there, each term adding one more order of correction: ∑k​Dkf(x0​)δk/k!.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1286Mutually exclusive eventsEvents that cannot happen at the same time; their intersection has probability 0.Note MA-017Independent and mutually exclusive events
G-1287n-gramA sequence of n consecutive words.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-1288n_binsThe KBinsDiscretizer parameter for the number of bins.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-1289n_componentsThe number of principal components PCA keeps; a number between 0 and 1 means a share of the variance.Note ML-048PCA
G-1291n_estimatorsThe number of base models in an ensemble.Note ML-100Ensemble learning
G-1290n_estimators (AdaBoost)The largest number of simple models (weak learners) AdaBoost builds, one per boosting round (stage).Note ML-112AdaBoost
G-1292n_initHow many times KMeans starts again from new starting centres (centroids); the run whose points sit closest to their centres (the lowest inertia) is kept.Note ML-123K-means
G-1293n_iterRandomizedSearchCV’s setting for how many hyperparameter combinations it draws at random and tries (default 10); trying a few instead of every combination makes the search much faster.Note ML-093Grid and random search
G-1294n_jobsscikit-learn setting for how many CPU cores to use in parallel; -1 means all.Note ML-098Voting ensembles
G-1295Nabla (∇)The upside-down triangle ∇, read “nabla” or “grad”; ∇f means the gradient of f, the vector that collects all its partial derivatives.Note MA-062Partial derivatives and gradients
G-1296Naive assumptionThe assumption that, within each class, the inputs are independent of each other (conditional independence given the class); it lets Naive Bayes multiply one probability per input instead of counting rare full combinations.Note ML-081Naive Bayes
G-1297Naive Bayes classifier (Naive Bayes)A classifier that applies Bayes’ theorem with the assumption that inputs are independent within each class.Note ML-081Naive Bayes
G-1299Name tokensThe tokens that spell the athlete’s name in a prompt such as “Michael Jordan plays the sport of”; zeroing the MLP outputs at these positions tests whether the MLPs there recall the sport.Note DL-089MLP blocks as fact storage
G-1300Named entity recognition (NER)Marking which words of a sentence are entities, specific things a program must act on, such as “7 pm” and “airport”; chatbots use it to pick out times and places.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1301named_stepsA pipeline’s dictionary from each step’s name to its object; used to reach one step and look inside it, for example when debugging.Note ML-028ML pipelines
G-1302nan-Euclidean distanceA distance between two rows that may have missing values: the Euclidean distance over only the columns both rows have, scaled up by (all columns / used columns) so rows with gaps do not look too close. scikit-learn uses it to find neighbours for KNN imputation.Note ML-038KNN imputer
G-1303Narrow AIAI that does one specific task. All AI today is narrow.Note ML-002Artificial intelligence
G-1304NaT”Not a time”: the missing value of a datetime column.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-1305Natural language processing (NLP)The part of ML that works with human language.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-1306Nearest neighbours (neighbours)The rows at the smallest distance from a given row; in KNN, the k training points closest to the query point.Note ML-038K-nearest neighbours
G-1307Nearly perpendicularTwo directions whose angle is close to 90 degrees, so their cosine (and dot product) is close to 0; letting feature directions be only nearly perpendicular lets a vector of d numbers store more than d features, at the price of a little interference.Note DL-090Superposition and nearly perpendicular directions
G-1308Negative gradientThe direction that lowers the loss fastest: minus the derivative of the loss with respect to the prediction.Note ML-115Gradient boosting
G-1309Negative hyperplane (π−)In an SVM, the copy of the separating hyperplane pushed out, parallel to it, until it touches the first negative-class point; with π+ on the other side it marks the edges of the margin.Note ML-086Support vector machines
G-1310Negative log-likelihood (NLL)The log-likelihood with its sign flipped, so a better fit gives a smaller number; fitting minimises it, which is the same as maximising the likelihood.Note MA-070Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1311Negative powerA power with a minus sign, which means one over the positive power: a−n=1/an, so 2−3=1/8.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-1312Negative skew (left skew)A long tail on the left: a few very small values.Note ML-019Skewness
G-1314NeocognitronAn early pattern-recognition network, built by Fukushima in 1980 from S-cells and C-cells; a forerunner of CNNs.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-2158Nested cross-validationA way to score a tuned model fairly: the whole tuning search runs inside each outer fold of cross-validation, so the chosen model is scored on data the search never saw.Note ML-106Cross-validation
G-1315Nesterov accelerated gradient (NAG)A version of momentum that first takes the momentum jump and then measures the gradient where it lands (the look-ahead point); seeing the slope ahead lets it brake before the minimum and swing less.Note DL-035Nesterov accelerated gradient (NAG)
G-1316Neural networkA model made of many simple connected units (neurons) in layers, loosely inspired by the brain; it learns the weights of its connections from data and is the model deep learning uses.Note ML-002Neural networks
G-1318Neuron (biological)A brain cell: dendrites take signals in, the nucleus processes them, the axon sends the result on.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-1317Neuron (in a network)One unit of a neural network (in an ANN, a perceptron): it takes inputs from the layer before, combines them with its learned weights and passes its output on.Note DL-002Neural networks
G-1319NeuroplasticityThe brain’s connections strengthening, weakening, vanishing or forming over time.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-1320Newton stepMinimising a function by fitting a parabola from its first and second derivatives and jumping to the parabola’s lowest point.Note ML-116Gradient boosting
G-1321Newton’s methodA way to find a minimum: at the current point, fit a bowl (the second-order Taylor polynomial, from the first and second derivatives), jump to its lowest point, and repeat; the step is δ=−H−1∇fT. XGBoost uses one such step for every tree.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1322Next-word predictorA model that takes some text and predicts the word that comes next.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-1324Node numberA node’s index in a fitted tree, counted depth-first from 0 at the root; dtreeviz can print it so a node in the picture can be found in the arrays of clf.tree_.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-1325Node-level feature sampling (node-level column sampling)Drawing a new random set of features before every split (random forest).Note ML-104Random forest
G-1326Noise (ε)The random part of a target that the model’s prediction does not explain.Note MA-072Log loss (binary cross entropy)
G-1327Noise (irreducible error)Randomness in the data that no model can predict.Note ML-061Bias-variance trade-off
G-1328Noise floorThe flat run of small singular values that random noise produces; the few singular values standing above it carry the real structure, so keeping only those removes most of the noise.Note MA-059Low-rank approximation (truncated SVD)
G-1329Noise pointIn DBSCAN, a point in a sparse area that is neither a core point nor a border point; it is treated as an outlier and labelled -1.Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-1330Nominal dataCategorical data whose categories have no order, such as states.Note ML-025Encoding categorical data
G-1331Non-autoregressiveProducing all output positions at once, as the decoder does during training.Note DL-084Transformer decoder
G-1332Non-closed-form solutionAn answer reached by improving a guess step by step.Note ML-050Gradient descent
G-1333Non-convex functionA function whose curve is not one simple bowl: some straight line between two of its points (a chord) lies below part of the curve. It can have several local minima.Note MA-065Convex and non-convex loss
G-1334Non-Gaussian distributionAny distribution that is not normal.Note MA-029Log-normal distribution
G-1335Non-linear dataData whose classes no straight line, plane or hyperplane can separate.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1336Non-linear variants of ReLUReLU variants with a curve on the negative side: ELU and SELU.Note DL-028Leaky ReLU, PReLU, ELU and SELU
G-1337Non-nullA cell that holds a value rather than a missing one; counting the non-null values of each column shows how much of it is missing.Note ML-018Exploratory data analysis
G-1338Non-parametric density estimationEstimating the shape of the data’s distribution (its PDF) straight from the data, without first assuming a shape such as the normal curve.Note MA-023Density estimation
G-1339Non-saturating functionA function with no ceiling on its output, so it does not flatten out, such as ReLU for positive inputs; its slope does not shrink to 0, which avoids the vanishing gradient that saturating functions cause.Note DL-027Activation functions
G-1340Non-sequential dataData whose features can be listed in any order without changing the meaning, such as a table row.Note DL-055Sequential data
G-1341Non-trainable parameterA stored number that gradient descent does not update, such as a moving mean.Note DL-031Batch normalisation
G-1343Normal distributionA symmetric, bell-shaped distribution: most values sit near the mean and they get rarer the further out we go; its mean and standard deviation set its centre and width.Note MA-024Normal distribution
G-1344Normal equationA formula that gives all linear-regression coefficients in one step, with no iterations (a closed-form solution): β=(XTX)−1XTy.Note ML-053Normal equation
G-1345Normal equationsA set of equations, one per coefficient, whose solution is the best-fit (least-squares) coefficients: XTXβ=XTy.Note ML-053Normal equation
G-1346Normal vectorA vector perpendicular to a line, plane or hyperplane; for wTx+w0​=0 it is w.Note MA-051Equation of a hyperplane
G-1348Normalisation (in a network)Transforming values so they have chosen statistics, usually mean 0 and variance 1; in a network it is applied to the inputs and hidden activations so they stay in a fixed range and training is more stable and faster.Note DL-080Layer normalisation
G-1347Normalisation (of weights)Dividing every weight by their sum so they add up to 1.Note ML-111AdaBoost
G-1349Normalization (feature scaling)The type of feature scaling that squeezes values into a fixed range, such as 0 to 1.Note ML-024Normalization
G-1350Normalized importancesImportances divided by their total, so they add up to 1.Note ML-108Feature importance
G-1351Normalizing inputsBringing every input column of a network to the same scale before training, by standardization or normalization; without it, the weights of large-valued inputs get huge gradients and training goes badly.Note DL-023Scaling inputs for neural networks
G-1352Not commutativeThe order of the factors matters: AB=BA in general.Note MA-054Matrix multiplication as composition
G-1353NotebookA .ipynb file of cells, each with its output underneath.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1354np.argminNumPy function returning the position of the smallest value.Note ML-124K-means
G-1355np.concatenateNumPy function that joins arrays; with axis=1 it puts them side by side.Note ML-027Column transformer
G-1356np.insertNumPy function that inserts values into an array at a given position.Note ML-054Normal equation
G-1357np.linalg.invNumPy function that computes the inverse of a square matrix.Note ML-054Normal equation
G-1358np.linalg.lstsqNumPy function that finds the best-fit answer to a set of linear equations, the one with the smallest squared error (the least-squares solution).Note ML-054Normal equation
G-1359NPUA neural processing unit: a chip in phones that speeds up networks.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-1360Nucleus (top p) samplingA sampling rule for text generation that keeps only the smallest set of most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to at least p, then samples among them; it cuts off the unlikely tail and adapts the cut to the context.Note DL-088Unembedding, logits, temperature and sampling
G-1361Null hypothesis (H0​)The statement of no effect, no difference or no relationship; assumed true until the data gives strong evidence against it.Note MA-038Hypothesis testing: null and alternative
G-1362Null spaceAll vectors a matrix sends to 0; spanned by the vi​ with σi​=0.Note MA-058Singular value decomposition
G-1363Nullable integer (Int64)The pandas integer type that can also hold a missing value, <NA>.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-1364Nullity matrixA picture of the whole table with each missing value drawn as a white line; it shows where values are missing and whether gaps in different columns fall in the same rows.Note ML-021Missing values
G-1365Number of samples (k)How many samples are drawn; different from the sample size n.Note MA-034Sampling distribution and standard error
G-1366Numerator layoutWriting derivatives with outputs as rows and inputs as columns.Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-2247Numeric understandingKnowing how to carry out a computation, such as a matrix product.Note MA-002How to learn the maths for ML
G-1367Numerical dataData made of numbers.Note ML-003Supervised learning
G-1368Numerical derivativeAn estimate of a derivative straight from its definition: the change in the function over a small step h, divided by h (a finite difference); a computer can get it from function values alone.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1369NumPyPython’s library for arrays and linear algebra.Note MA-047Linear algebra roadmap
G-1373Objective (Keras Tuner)The metric the tuner maximises or minimises, such as val_accuracy.Note DL-039Keras Tuner
G-1372Objective functionThe quantity an algorithm tries to make as large or as small as possible.Note ML-047PCA
G-1370Objective function (Optuna)The function a search optimises: it takes a trial’s hyperparameter values and returns a score.Note ML-128Optuna
G-1371Objective function (XGBoost)The quantity XGBoost minimises: the loss plus a regularisation term.Note ML-120XGBoost
G-1374ObservationOne record of a dataset: one row of the data table.Note ML-003Supervised learning
G-1375Observed count OThe number of sample rows in a category or table cell.Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-1376OddsHow often an event happens divided by how often it does not, e.g. 5 placed to 3 not placed is 5/3.Note ML-116Gradient boosting
G-1377Offline learningTraining a model once on all the data away from the live system, for example on the engineer’s own machine, and then deploying it; another name for batch learning.Note ML-004Batch (offline) learning
G-1378OLTPOnline transaction processing: the database that records every action as it happens.Note ML-013Framing an ML problem
G-1379One-hot encodingReplacing a nominal column by one 0/1 column per category, with a single 1 in each row; also used to represent words.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-1380One-hot targetA target with probability 1 on the correct word and 0 on all others.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-1381One-sample proportion testA test of whether the share (proportion) of one category in the population equals a claimed value π0​, using a z statistic (a z-test).Note MA-044One-sample proportion test
G-1382One-sample t-testA test of whether a population’s mean equals a claimed value, from one sample, when the population standard deviation σ is unknown: t=(xˉ−μ0​)/(s/n​).Note MA-042T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1383One-sided and two-sided critical valueThe cut-off beyond which the test statistic leads to rejecting H0​ (the critical value): one-sided puts the whole α in one tail, two-sided puts α/2 in each of the two tails.Note MA-039Z-test and rejection regions
G-1384One-tailed p-valueThe p-value counted on one side only: the tail area beyond the test statistic on the side that H1​ points to.Note MA-041P-values
G-1385One-tailed test (one-sided test)A test whose H1​ has a direction (> or <), with the whole rejection region in one tail.Note MA-040Type I and II errors, power, tails
G-1386One-to-many RNNAn RNN that takes one non-sequential input and produces a sequence.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1387One-to-oneA network with non-sequential input and output: an ordinary ANN or CNN, not an RNN.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1388One-vs-restTraining one binary classifier per class, each separating that class from all others.Note ML-078Softmax regression
G-1389One-way ANOVAA test of whether three or more group means are equal, with the groups defined by one categorical column.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-1390OneHotEncoderscikit-learn’s class for one-hot encoding; remembers the categories it learned.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-1391Online learningTraining incrementally on mini-batches while the model is live in production.Note ML-005Online learning
G-1392OOB predictionA prediction for a training row made only by the trees that never saw that row, because their random sample (bootstrap sample) missed it.Note ML-107OOB score
G-1393oob_decision_function_Each training row’s class probabilities, given only by the trees that never saw that row (its OOB trees).Note ML-107OOB score
G-1394oob_prediction_For a regressor, each training row’s prediction from only the trees that never saw it (its OOB prediction).Note ML-107OOB score
G-1395oob_score_The accuracy (classifier) or R2 (regressor) of each training row’s prediction by the trees that never saw it (the OOB predictions).Note ML-107OOB score
G-1396OPTICSA density-based clustering algorithm, like DBSCAN: it groups points that lie in dense areas, so clusters can have any shape (Ankerst et al. 1999).Note ML-126DBSCAN
G-1397Optimal number of featuresThe number of columns at which a model performs best.Note ML-045Curse of dimensionality
G-1400OptimisationChanging a model step by step until its error is as small as possible.Note MA-001Role of mathematics in ML
G-1398Optimisation algorithmA method for finding the parameter values that make a function as small (or large) as possible.Note ML-056Gradient descent
G-1399Optimisation problemFinding the inputs (here the weights and biases) that make a function (here the loss) smallest.Note DL-032Optimizers in deep learning
G-1401OptimizerThe rule that turns gradients into weight updates, such as plain gradient descent or Adam.Note DL-021Optimizers in deep learning
G-1402OptunaA Python framework for hyperparameter tuning that uses the results of earlier tries to pick the next values to test (Bayesian optimisation).Note ML-128Optuna
G-1403Ordinal dataCategorical data whose categories have a natural order, such as Poor < Average < Good.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-1404Ordinal encodingReplacing ordered categories by 0, 1, 2, … in their order; for input columns.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-1405OrdinalEncoderscikit-learn’s class for ordinal encoding; takes the order through categories.Note ML-025Ordinal and label encoding
G-1406Ordinary least squares (OLS, least squares)The way linear regression finds its line with one formula (a closed-form method): the line with the smallest sum of squared errors.Note ML-050Ordinary least squares (closed form)
G-2251OrientationWhich side of ^ the vector ^​ lies on; a transformation that swaps the sides flips the plane over and has a negative determinant.Note MA-063Determinant
G-2240OriginThe point where the axes cross; the tail of every vector in linear algebra.Note MA-048Vectors and feature vectors
G-1408OrthogonalAt right angles (perpendicular); two non-zero vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is 0, which as data means they share nothing.Note MA-050Dot product
G-1407Orthogonal matrixA square matrix that only rotates or flips: its columns have length 1 and are all perpendicular (orthonormal), and its inverse is its transpose.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1409OrthonormalVectors of length 1 that are all perpendicular to each other.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1410OscillationSwinging back and forth past the minimum before settling.Note DL-035SGD with momentum
G-1411Out-of-bag (OOB) evaluation, OOB scoreTesting a bagging model by predicting each training row with only the base models that never saw it; the OOB score is the accuracy (or R2) of those predictions.Note ML-107OOB score
G-1412Out-of-bag observations (out-of-bag rows)The observations a base model never saw because its bootstrap sample missed them (about 37%).Note ML-107OOB score
G-1413Out-of-core learning (out-of-core computing)Training on data too big for the memory (RAM) by loading it chunk by chunk, offline.Note ML-005Out-of-core learning
G-1415Out-of-fold predictionA prediction for a row made by a model trained on the other folds, never on that row.Note ML-121Stacking and blending
G-1416Out-of-vocabulary (OOV) tokenA placeholder token, [UNK], that stands for every word not in the vocabulary, so a word never seen in training still gets an index.Note DL-057Tokenization and integer encoding of text
G-1417OutcomeThe single result of one trial, such as heads or a 3.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-1418Outer productMultiplying a column vector by a row vector to get a whole matrix: δδT has entry δi​δj​ for every pair; it is what δ2 means in a Taylor polynomial of several variables.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1420OutlierA value far from the rest of the data.Note ML-019Outliers
G-1419Outlier detectionFinding the values that lie far from the rest of a feature: compute a lower and an upper limit, and flag every value outside them as an outlier, ready to be removed or changed.Note ML-040Outliers
G-1422Output gate (ot​)The LSTM gate that decides how much of the cell’s memory to show as the new hidden state: a sigmoid layer gives ot​, between 0 and 1, which scales tanh(ct​) to give ht​.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-1424Output layerThe last layer, which gives the prediction.Note DL-002Neural networks
G-1425Output value (classification)The number a leaf of an XGBoost classification tree adds to the prediction, in log-odds: sum of residuals / (∑p(1−p)+λ), with p the previous predicted probabilities.Note ML-119XGBoost
G-1426Output value (leaf weight)The number an XGBoost regression leaf predicts: sum of residuals / (number of residuals + λ); with λ=0 it is the mean residual, and a larger λ pulls it towards 0.Note ML-118XGBoost
G-1427Output-size formulaThe rule that gives the size of a convolution’s output from the image size n, filter size f, padding p and stride s: ⌊(n+2p−f)/s⌋+1.Note DL-043Padding and strides
G-1428OverdispersionCounts that are much more spread out than their mean suggests (variance clearly larger than the mean), a sign that a Poisson model does not fit.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-1429OverfittingLearning the training data too closely, noise included; fails on new data.Note ML-007Overfitting
G-1430OvershootingMoving past the minimum because of the built-up velocity, then swinging back.Note DL-034SGD with momentum
G-1433P-valueThe probability, assuming H0​ is true, of getting a sample as or more extreme than ours.Note MA-041P-values
G-1431P-value approachCarrying out a test by computing a p-value, which also measures the strength of the evidence.Note MA-038P-values
G-1432P-value decision ruleReject H0​ if p≤α, otherwise fail to reject it.Note MA-041P-values
G-1435PackageA library bundled so that a package manager such as pip or conda can download and install it.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1434Package managerA program that downloads and installs libraries in versions that fit together.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1436PaddingAdding zeros to sequences so that all have the same length.Note DL-057Sequence padding
G-1437Pair plotA grid of scatter plots of every pair of numerical columns, with histograms on the diagonal.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-1438Paired observationsTwo measurements that belong to the same subject or matched pair.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1439Paired t-test (dependent t-test)A test of whether two linked measurements of the same subjects differ on average; it works on the difference within each pair (a t-test on the differences).Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1440Pandas ProfilingA library that builds a full EDA report (column summaries, missing values, correlations and more) from a DataFrame in a few lines of code; now named fg-data-profiling.Note ML-021Pandas Profiling
G-1441pandas, DataFramePython’s main table library, and its name for a table.Note ML-012Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1442Parallel corpusA dataset of sentences paired with their translations, one pair per row; it is the training data of a translation model.Note DL-068Sequence-to-sequence (encoder-decoder)
G-1443Parallel learningTraining the base models independently, so they can all be trained at once (bagging).Note ML-113Ensemble learning
G-1444Parallel processingSplitting one job among several processor cores working at the same time.Note ML-117XGBoost
G-1445Parallel trainingTraining in which all positions of a sequence are computed at the same time.Note DL-071Transformer
G-1448Parameter (of a function)A named setting passed to a function, like sep=";".Note ML-014CSV files
G-2276Parameter (of a population)A number that describes the whole population, such as its true mean μ; it is usually unknown, so we estimate it from a sample statistic.Note MA-004Population, sample, parameter and statistic
G-1446Parameter gridA dictionary that lists the model settings to tune (hyperparameter names) and the values to try for each.Note ML-106Grid and random search
G-1447Parameter sharingUsing the same weights at every position or time step; it lets a model handle sequences of any length and recognise a pattern wherever it appears.Note DL-055Parameter sharing across time steps
G-1449Parameters (of a distribution)The numbers, such as μ and σ, that set a distribution’s location, scale and shape.Note MA-020Probability distributions
G-1450Parameters (of a model)The numbers inside a model that training learns from the data, such as a line’s slope and intercept; once learned, they turn inputs into predictions.Note ML-006Model-based learning
G-1451Parametric density estimationEstimating how the data is spread (its probability density) by assuming it follows a named distribution and estimating that distribution’s parameters from the data.Note MA-023Density estimation
G-1452Parametric ReLU (PReLU)An activation that passes positive inputs unchanged and multiplies negative ones by a small slope a that is learned during training, one per node (a Leaky ReLU with a learned slope).Note DL-028Leaky ReLU, PReLU, ELU and SELU
G-1453Pareto distributionA distribution of values that start at a smallest value xm​ and become rarer the larger they are, in a long right tail (a right-skewed power law); used to model wealth and income. PDF αxmα​/xα+1.Note MA-030Pareto distribution and power laws
G-1454Parse, parserRead text and build a structure from it; the part that does this.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-1456Part-of-speech taggingLabelling every word of a sentence with its part of speech.Note DL-058Types of RNN (many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)
G-1457Partial derivativeThe slope of a function of several variables in one variable, holding the others fixed.Note ML-050Partial derivatives and gradients
G-1458partial_fitA scikit-learn method that continues training from where the model left off.Note ML-005Online learning
G-1459PartitionA set of events of which exactly one happens in every trial: no two can happen together (mutually exclusive) and together they cover every outcome (exhaustive).Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-1460passthrough (ColumnTransformer)The remainder option that keeps untouched columns unchanged.Note ML-027Column transformer
G-1461Passthrough (stacking)In stacking, giving the final model that combines the base models (the meta-model) the original input columns as well as the base models’ predictions.Note ML-121Stacking and blending
G-1462Past defaultersPast borrowers who did not repay their loan; a loan model compares a new applicant with them, and high similarity means high risk.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-1463PastingTraining several models, each on its own random sample of rows drawn without replacement (no row twice), and combining their predictions; it is bagging with this sample instead of a bootstrap sample.Note ML-100Bagging
G-1464Path (in a network)A route from a node to the output along connections; a derivative sums its products over all paths.Note DL-019Backpropagation
G-1465Path (in the chain rule)One route through the computation from the loss to a weight; the derivative is the sum over all paths.Note DL-059Backpropagation through time (BPTT)
G-1466PatienceHow many passes over the training data (epochs) in a row without improvement training waits before early stopping ends it.Note DL-022Early stopping
G-1467PatternThe relationship between input and output that the algorithm discovers.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-2169Pattern recognitionFinding regularities in data; the measurable part of intelligence that today’s AI covers.Note ML-002Artificial intelligence
G-1469PCA (principal component analysis)A way to replace many columns with a few new ones that keep most of the spread in the data, using no labels (unsupervised feature extraction for dimensionality reduction). Each new column, a principal component, follows one direction of greatest variance. Used to cut the number of features and to plot data with many columns.Note ML-046PCA
G-1468PCA through the SVDComputing PCA from the SVD of the centred data: the columns of V are the principal components, σi2​/n their variances, and UΣ the data’s new coordinates (scores).Note MA-060Singular value decomposition
G-1470pd.crosstabpandas function that counts how often each pair of values from two columns occurs.Note ML-083Naive Bayes
G-1471pd.cutThe pandas function that puts values into intervals we give it.Note ML-031Binning and binarization
G-1472pd.to_datetimeThe pandas function that converts text to datetime values.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-1473pd.to_numericThe pandas function that converts values to numbers.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-1474Pearson correlation coefficient (Pearson’s r)The usual measure of correlation for linear (straight-line) relationships between two numerical columns, written r; the one df.corr() computes.Note ML-018Correlation
G-1475Pearson’s skewness coefficientA simple measure of skew: three times the gap between the mean and the median, divided by the standard deviation, 3(xˉ−median)/s; positive for right skew, negative for left.Note MA-026Skewness
G-1477penaltyThe SGDRegressor setting that chooses how large weights are penalised (regularisation), such as “l2” for Ridge.Note ML-064Ridge regression
G-1476Penalty termThe extra term added to the cost to discourage large weights.Note DL-026L1 and L2 regularisation in neural networks
G-1478penalty=NoneThe LogisticRegression setting that switches off the penalty on large weights (regularisation).Note ML-074Logistic regression
G-1479Per-row seedA seed taken from a row’s own values, so the same input always gets the same random fill.Note ML-037Random sample imputation
G-1483PercentileThe value below which a given share of the data lies.Note ML-018Percentile outlier method
G-2234Percentile bootstrap intervalA range for a population value built by resampling: draw many resamples with replacement from one sample, compute each one’s mean, and keep the middle 95% (2.5th to 97.5th percentile); it works for any statistic, even with no formula.Note MA-035Confidence intervals
G-1480Percentile locationWhere the p-th percentile sits in sorted data: position (p/100)×(n+1); if it falls between two values, the percentile lies the same fraction of the way between them.Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-1481Percentile method (percentile rule)A way to find outliers: flag values below a low percentile or above a high one (e.g. 1st and 99th); it works for any column.Note ML-043Percentile outlier method
G-1482Percentile rankThe percentile a given value falls at: the values below it plus half of those equal to it, as a share of all values, (X+0.5Y)/n×100.Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-1486PerceptronThe smallest building block of a neural network, one artificial neuron: it multiplies each input by a weight, adds the results and turns the sum into an output.Note DL-004Perceptron
G-1484Perceptron lossA loss for the perceptron that is 0 for a point on its correct side and ∣f(x)∣ for a point on the wrong side, so worse mistakes cost more: max(0,−yf(x)) per point, labels ±1. Minimising it trains the line.Note DL-006Perceptron loss
G-1485Perceptron trickMoving a line towards each misclassified point until the classes are separated.Note ML-069Perceptron trick
G-1487Perfect separationWhen a line splits the training classes with no mistakes; unregularised weights then grow without limit.Note ML-074Logistic regression
G-1489Periodic functionA function that repeats after a fixed interval, its period.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-1490Permutation importanceA feature’s importance measured as the drop in a model’s test score when that column’s values are shuffled; a big drop means the model relies on it, and unlike impurity-based importance it is not fooled by columns with many unique values.Note ML-108Permutation importance
G-1491permutation_importancescikit-learn function (in sklearn.inspection) that computes permutation importance.Note ML-108Permutation importance
G-1492PerplexityA score of how surprised a language model is by the correct tokens: the exponential of the mean cross-entropy per token; lower means it gave the correct tokens higher probability.Note DL-086Label smoothing
G-1493phpMyAdminA web page for creating and managing MySQL databases.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-1494pickleA Python module that saves objects to a file and loads them back.Note ML-012Saving models with pickle
G-1495Pie chartA circle split into slices sized by each category’s share.Note ML-019Univariate analysis
G-1496Piecewise linearMade of straight segments joined at bends; the shape of a ReLU network’s decision boundary.Note DL-026L1 and L2 regularisation in neural networks
G-1497pipPython’s own package manager, which installs from PyPI.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1499PipelineOne object that chains preprocessing steps and a model, each step’s output feeding the next; every input, including new ones after deployment, then gets exactly the same preprocessing.Note ML-028ML pipelines
G-1498Pipeline (class)The scikit-learn class (in sklearn.pipeline) that builds a pipeline from a list of (name, object) tuples.Note ML-028ML pipelines
G-2161Pipeline mapA diagram of the 14 steps of an ML project, from framing the problem to deployment, that shows where each Concept belongs.Course map
G-1500Pivot tableA grid with one column’s values as rows, another’s as columns, and a third in the cells.Note ML-020Bivariate and multivariate analysis
G-1501PixelOne dot of an image, stored as one or more numbers.Note ML-010Tensors
G-1502PlaneA flat surface in 3D; the model for two input columns.Note ML-052Multiple linear regression
G-1503PlateauA nearly flat region of the loss, where steps become very small.Note ML-056Gradient descent
G-1504PlatykurticA distribution with thinner tails than the normal, so fewer extreme values; its excess kurtosis is below 0.Note MA-028Kurtosis and moments
G-1505PlausibilityHow believable a parameter value is in the light of the data; measured by its likelihood relative to other values.Note MA-069Likelihood
G-1506Plural directionA direction in embedding space: the average of the arrows from singular to plural nouns, scaled to length 1; a word’s dot product with it scores how plural the word is.Note DL-072Meaning as direction in embedding space
G-1507Point estimateA single number computed from sample data as the best guess for an unknown population parameter.Note MA-034Confidence intervals
G-1508Pointwise operationAn operation done entry by entry on vectors of the same length, such as ⊙.Note DL-062LSTM gates (forget, input, output) and cell state
G-1509Poisson distributionA distribution that gives the probability of each possible count of events (0, 1, 2, …) in a fixed interval of time or space, from the average count λ; used for counts such as questions per day.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-1510Poisson regressionA model for a count target, such as bike rentals per hour: it predicts the average count λ for each row from its features, and the Poisson distribution then gives the probability of each count.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-1511Polar coordinatesDescribing a point by its distance r from the origin and its angle θ: (rcosθ,rsinθ).Note MA-063Jacobian and matrix gradients
G-1512PolicyThe agent’s rules for which action to take.Note ML-003Reinforcement learning
G-1513Polynomial featuresNew input columns made from powers and products of the original inputs, such as x12​ and x1​x2​; they let a linear model fit curves and curved decision boundaries.Note ML-079Polynomial features
G-1514Polynomial kernelA function that gives the dot product of two points after their inputs are expanded into powers, such as x2 (a kernel whose feature map is built from powers of the inputs); it lets an SVM draw curved boundaries.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1515Polynomial regressionLinear regression on powers (and products) of the inputs, to fit curves.Note ML-060Polynomial regression
G-1516PolynomialFeaturesscikit-learn transformer that creates the power and product columns.Note ML-060Polynomial features
G-1517Polysemantic neuronA neuron that responds to several unrelated features.Note DL-090Superposition and nearly perpendicular directions
G-1518PolytopeThe region where a set of linear inequalities all hold, such as the feasible region of a linear program: a polygon in two dimensions.Note MA-068Linear and quadratic programming
G-1519Pooled standard deviationThe combined standard deviation of two groups used by Student’s two-sample t-test.Note MA-043T-tests: one-sample, two-sample, paired
G-1521PoolingReplacing each small window of a feature map with one summary number, to shrink the map.Note DL-044Pooling
G-1520Pooling layerA CNN layer that shrinks the feature map from a convolution layer by replacing each small window with one number, such as its maximum; this cuts the computation and makes the features less sensitive to small shifts.Note DL-044Pooling
G-1525PopulationThe entire group of individuals or objects we want to study.Note MA-004Population, sample, parameter and statistic
G-1522Population correlation ρThe correlation between two columns in the whole population; r estimates it.Note MA-044Correlation significance test
G-1523Population covariance (σxy​)The covariance computed from every member of a population: the average product of the two columns’ distances from their means, dividing by N; it shows whether the two columns move together.Note MA-009Covariance and covariance matrix
G-1524Population mean (μ)The mean of every value in the population.Note MA-005Measures of central tendency
G-1526Position embedding matrix WP​A learned table with one vector per position in the text (1,024 rows in GPT-2); a token’s position row is added to its token embedding, so the model knows where the token sits.Note DL-087Decoder-only GPT
G-1527Position-wiseApplied to each word’s vector separately, with the same weights for every position.Note DL-081Transformer encoder
G-1528Positional encodingA vector added to each word’s embedding that tells the model the word’s position.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-1529Positive and negative sideThe two halves of the plane on either side of a line Ax+By+C=0: where Ax+By+C is above 0 and where it is below 0; the perceptron predicts one class on each side.Note ML-069Logistic regression
G-1530Positive definite matrixA symmetric matrix that curves upward in every direction: its eigenvalues are all positive, and its quadratic form is a strictly convex bowl.Note MA-068Linear and quadratic programming
G-1531Positive hyperplane (π+)A copy of the separating hyperplane moved out, parallel to itself, until it touches the first positive point; with the negative hyperplane it marks the two edges of the SVM’s margin.Note ML-086Support vector machines
G-1532Positive semi-definiteA symmetric matrix that never curves downward in any direction: its eigenvalues are all 0 or positive. For such a matrix the eigenvectors are orthonormal, so its eigen-decomposition and its SVD are the same.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1533Positive skew (right skew)A long tail on the right: a few very large values.Note ML-019Skewness
G-1534Post-hoc testA test run after ANOVA rejects, to find which groups differ.Note MA-046One-way ANOVA
G-1536PosteriorThe probability of an event after the evidence is taken into account.Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-1535Posterior p(θ∣data)The distribution over the parameters after seeing the data; proportional to likelihood × prior.Note MA-072MAP estimation
G-1537Power iterationFinding the top eigenvector by multiplying a vector by the matrix again and again.Note MA-056Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
G-1538Power lawA relationship y=kxa: one variable proportional to a power of the other.Note MA-030Pareto distribution and power laws
G-1539Power of a testThe probability that a test detects a real effect, that is, rejects H0​ when H0​ is false; it equals 1−β, where β is the probability of a Type II error.Note MA-040Type I and II errors, power, tails
G-1540Power ruleThe rule for differentiating a power of x: bring the power down in front and lower the power by one, (xn)′=nxn−1.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1541Power seriesA polynomial with infinitely many terms, ∑ak​(x−c)k; the Taylor series is one example, and it lets functions such as ex and sinx be computed from polynomials.Note MA-061Taylor series
G-1542Power transformerA transform that raises each column to a learned power λ to make it close to normal.Note ML-030Power transformer
G-1543PowerTransformerscikit-learn’s class that applies the Box-Cox or Yeo-Johnson power transform to each column, to make its distribution closer to normal.Note ML-030Power transformer
G-1544PPMIPositive pointwise mutual information: a score of how much more often two words appear together than by chance, with negative scores set to 0.Note DL-073Word embeddings
G-1545Pre-LN transformer (prenorm)A transformer variant with layer normalisation at the input of each sub-layer, inside the residual branch, instead of after the addition; it trains without warm-up.Note DL-086Layer normalisation
G-1546Pre-trainingThe first, general training of a model on a large dataset, such as ImageNet or a huge amount of unlabelled text, so that it learns general features; fine-tuning then adapts it to a task with little labelled data.Note DL-067Transfer learning (feature extraction and fine-tuning)
G-1547PrecisionOf all items predicted positive, the fraction that really are positive.Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-1548Predict (prediction, inference)Use a trained model to give an answer for new data it has not seen, with no correct output available.Note ML-002Machine learning
G-1549predict_probascikit-learn method that returns predicted probabilities instead of classes.Note ML-077ROC curve and AUC
G-1550Prediction (y^​)The value the model gives for an input whose true output is not known; the hat marks a prediction.Note ML-050Best-fit line and squared error
G-1552Prediction pathThe nodes a row passes through, from the root to the leaf that predicts it.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-1553Predictive maintenanceRepairing a machine before it breaks, based on predicted faults.Note ML-008Applications of ML
G-1554Preferred stimulusThe pattern, such as an edge of one orientation, that a cell responds to most.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1555PrefixThe first few words of a sentence; in next-word prediction each prefix is one training input and the word that follows it is the target.Note DL-063Next-word prediction with an LSTM
G-1558Pretrained modelA network already trained by someone else on a large dataset, reused for our own predictions.Note DL-051Pretrained models and ImageNet
G-1559Primal problemThe original constrained optimisation problem, in its own variables x; it is called primal to tell it apart from the dual problem built from it with Lagrange multipliers.Note MA-066Lagrange multipliers, KKT and duality
G-1560Primary visual cortex (V1)The first area of the cortex that processes visual signals.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1561Primitive featureA basic feature such as an edge, found by the first layers.Note DL-040Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1563Principal componentA new axis found by PCA, a direction through the data: PC1 holds the most variance, PC2 the next most at right angles to it; keeping only the first few cuts the number of features.Note ML-046PCA
G-1565PriorThe probability of an event before any evidence is seen.Note MA-018Bayes’ theorem
G-1564Prior p(θ)A distribution over the parameters expressing what we believe before seeing data.Note MA-072MAP estimation
G-1566Probabilistic interpretationReading the model’s output as the probability of the positive class.Note ML-071Logistic regression
G-1567Probabilistic modelA model that gives a probability for every possible target value, p(y∣x,θ), instead of a single predicted value.Note MA-072Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)
G-1574ProbabilityA number from 0 to 1 measuring how likely an event is; written P(A).Note MA-011Empirical vs theoretical probability, probability rules
G-1569Probability densityThe height of a continuous distribution’s curve; compares how likely nearby values are.Note MA-022Probability density function (PDF)
G-1568Probability density function (PDF)A curve showing how likely each value is; areas under it are probabilities.Note MA-022Probability density function (PDF)
G-1571Probability distributionA list of every possible outcome of a random variable with its probability.Note MA-020Probability distributions
G-1570Probability distribution functionA formula y=f(x) giving the probability of each outcome; the umbrella term for PMF and PDF.Note MA-020Probability distributions
G-1572Probability mass function (PMF)The function that gives the probability of each exact value of a discrete random variable, such as P(X=3)=1/6 for a fair die; its probabilities add up to 1.Note MA-021Probability mass function (PMF)
G-1573Probability treeA diagram that draws each stage of a problem as branches labelled with probabilities; multiplying along a path gives that path’s probability, and adding paths gives a total probability.Note MA-019Bayes’ theorem
G-1575ProbeA fixed direction used to score words: the dot product of a word’s vector with it.Note DL-072Meaning as direction in embedding space
G-1577Product ruleThe rule for the derivative of a product of two functions: differentiate one factor at a time, keep the other, and add: (fg)′=f′g+fg′.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1576Product rule for independent eventsFor independent events, the probability that both happen is the product of their separate probabilities: P(A∩B)=P(A)×P(B).Note MA-016Independent and mutually exclusive events
G-1578Production codeThe code that runs the deployed model on a server, for example behind a website.Note ML-028ML pipelines
G-1579Production environmentThe server where a model serves real users.Note ML-004Deployment
G-1580Profiling reportAn automatic EDA report describing every column and pair of columns of a dataset.Note ML-021Pandas Profiling
G-1581ProgramLogic written by us that turns an input into an output.Note ML-001Machine learning
G-1583ProjectionDropping a point or vector straight onto an axis, a line or another vector’s direction, like casting a shadow.Note ML-046PCA
G-1582Projection view of the dot productReading the dot product as a shadow: v⋅w is the signed length of w‘s shadow (projection) on the line of v times the length ∥v∥, negative when the shadow points away from v.Note MA-055Dot product
G-1584Proportional to (∝)Equal up to a constant factor, written ∝; in Naive Bayes the evidence term is the same for every class, so it is dropped and the classes are compared with ∝.Note ML-082Naive Bayes
G-1585Proximity matrixAn n × n table of the distances between every pair of points or clusters.Note ML-125Hierarchical clustering
G-1587PruningStopping a tree early or cutting it back so it does not overfit.Note ML-092Decision trees
G-1586Pruning (Optuna)Stopping an unpromising trial early, before its training finishes.Note ML-128Optuna
G-1588Pruning, quantization, knowledge distillationWays to make a model smaller: remove weights, store them with fewer bits, or train a small model to imitate a large one.Note DL-071Transformer
G-1589Pseudo-residualThe mistake on one row that the next tree learns; for squared error it is actual minus predicted.Note ML-114Gradient boosting
G-1590Public datasetA labelled dataset released for anyone to use.Note DL-002What deep learning is
G-1591Pure leafA leaf whose training rows all belong to one class.Note ML-094Decision trees
G-1592Push and pullMoving the line away from a correctly classified point, or towards a misclassified one.Note ML-071Logistic regression
G-1593PyPIThe Python Package Index, the public store of Python packages.Note ML-011Setup: conda, Jupyter and Colab
G-1594Pyramid structureHidden layers with fewer neurons in each later layer, such as 64-32-16; an old rule of thumb, not needed.Note DL-021Improving a neural network
G-1595PyTorchMeta’s deep learning library, most used in research.Note DL-001What deep learning is
G-1596Q-Q plotA plot of a column’s sorted values against the values a theoretical distribution, often the normal, would have; points on the line mean the data follows it.Note ML-029Q-Q plot
G-2252Quadratic approximationA curved surface that matches a function near a point in value, slopes and bending: the tangent plane plus the terms 21​fxx​δx2​+fxy​δx​δy​+21​fyy​δy2​; it is the second-order Taylor polynomial, and Newton’s method steps to its minimum.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1597Quadratic formAn expression such as xTAx that turns a vector into one number made only of squared entries and products of pairs of entries, such as x12​+3x22​; it is the curved part of a quadratic program’s objective.Note MA-068Linear and quadratic programming
G-1598Quadratic programA problem of finding the lowest point of a bowl-shaped function with squared terms (a convex quadratic) while meeting limits written as linear inequalities (constraints).Note MA-068Linear and quadratic programming
G-1599QuantilesValues that cut sorted data into equal-sized groups; a fraction p of the values lie below the quantile Q(p).Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-1600QuantileTransformerA scikit-learn transformer that maps each column’s values, through their quantiles, onto a uniform or normal distribution; it is used much less than the log and power transforms.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1601QuarterOne of four three-month parts of a year.Note ML-033Date and time features
G-1602QuartilesThe 25%, 50% and 75% percentiles, which cut the data into four equal groups.Note ML-018Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-1603Quasi-Newton methodNewton’s method with the Hessian replaced by a stand-in matrix built from how the gradient changes between steps, so no second derivatives are computed; BFGS and L-BFGS are examples.Note MA-064Hessian and multivariate Taylor
G-1606Query (SQL)A request for data, written in SQL.Note ML-015JSON and SQL data
G-1604Query parametersSettings written after the ? in an API’s URL and joined by &, such as page=1 or the API key; they tell the API which data to return.Note ML-016APIs
G-1605Query pointThe new point whose class we want to predict.Note ML-085K-nearest neighbours
G-1607Query, key, value vectorsThree vectors made from each word’s embedding by learned matrices: a word’s query is compared with every word’s key by dot products to get attention weights, and those weights mix the value vectors into the word’s new vector.Note DL-078Self-attention (query, key, value)
G-1608QuintilesThe 20th, 40th, 60th and 80th percentiles: cuts into 5 groups.Note MA-008Percentiles, quartiles and box plots
G-1609Quotient ruleThe rule for the derivative of a fraction of two functions: (f/g)′=(f′g−fg′)/g2.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1610Random experimentAn experiment whose outcome cannot be predicted, such as a coin toss.Note MA-010Events and sample spaces
G-1611Random forestBagging with decision trees as the base models: many trees, each trained on a random sample of the rows with a random choice of features at every split, vote (classification) or are averaged (regression), which lowers the variance of a single tree.Note ML-102Random forest
G-1612Random initializationStarting a model’s parameters at random values, often drawn from a uniform distribution.Note MA-029Weight initialisation
G-1613Random oversamplingCopying randomly chosen minority rows until the classes are equal.Note ML-127Random under- and oversampling
G-1614Random patchesTraining several models, each on a random subset of rows and a random subset of columns, and combining their predictions (a kind of bagging).Note ML-100Bagging
G-1615Random preprocessing layerA Keras layer, such as RandomFlip, that changes images at random during training and does nothing at prediction.Note DL-050Data augmentation
G-1616Random sample imputationFilling each gap with a value drawn at random from the column’s known values.Note ML-037Random sample imputation
G-1617Random seedA number that fixes a random number generator so that a run can be repeated exactly.Note ML-111Random sample imputation
G-1618Random subspacesTraining several models, each on all rows but a random subset of columns, and combining their predictions (a kind of bagging).Note ML-100Bagging
G-1619Random undersamplingDropping randomly chosen majority rows until the classes are equal.Note ML-127Random under- and oversampling
G-1620Random variableThe possible numerical outcomes of a random experiment; strictly, a function from outcomes to numbers.Note MA-020Random variables
G-1621RandomForestClassifierscikit-learn’s random forest for classification.Note ML-102Random forest
G-1622RandomForestRegressorscikit-learn’s random forest for regression.Note ML-102Random forest
G-1623Randomised controlled trialAn experiment that assigns a treatment at random, to test causation.Note MA-009Correlation and causation
G-1624Randomized SVDA fast method that finds only the top k singular vectors, used by scikit-learn for large data.Note MA-060Latent semantic analysis
G-1625RandomizedSearchCVA scikit-learn tool that tries a fixed number of randomly drawn combinations of model settings (hyperparameters) and scores each with cross-validation, instead of trying every combination.Note ML-093Grid and random search
G-1626RangeThe simplest measure of spread: the largest value minus the smallest.Note MA-006Variance
G-1630Rank k approximation (truncated SVD)The approximation of a matrix that keeps only its k largest singular values with their vectors and drops the rest, A^k​=Uk​Σk​VkT​; it is the best small summary of the matrix and needs far fewer numbers.Note MA-059Low-rank approximation (truncated SVD)
G-1627Rank (of a matrix)The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, that is, how many directions its columns really span; a column that is a combination of others does not add to it.Note MA-058Linear combinations, span and basis
G-1629Rank (of a tensor)The number of axes of a tensor (ndim in NumPy).Note ML-010Tensors
G-1628Rank collapseAll word vectors of a sentence becoming the same vector after many attention layers without residual connections.Note DL-081Residual connections and add & norm
G-1631Rank-1 layerOne piece of a matrix split by the SVD: a column times a row, σi​ui​viT​, weighted by its singular value σi​; adding all the layers gives back the matrix.Note MA-059Singular value decomposition
G-1632RapidAPIA website listing many APIs, including free ones.Note ML-016APIs
G-1633Rate λThe average number of events per interval; the only parameter of the Poisson distribution.Note MA-032Poisson distribution
G-1634Rate limitThe most requests an API accepts in a given time.Note ML-016APIs
G-1635Rate of changeHow much one quantity changes per unit change of another; the meaning of a derivative.Note MA-061Derivatives of one variable
G-1636Rate parameter λThe average number of events per unit time; the average wait is 1/λ.Note MA-071Exponential distribution
G-1637Raw dataData as it arrives, before any preparation.Note ML-022Feature engineering
G-1638Raw stringA Python string written r"...", in which a backslash is kept as it is.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-1639RBF kernelRadial basis function kernel, built on e−(distance)2: it scores two points as similar (close to 1) when they are near each other and close to 0 when far apart; the usual first-choice SVM kernel for curved boundaries.Note ML-089Kernel trick
G-1640ReaderWhat read_csv returns with chunksize: it hands out one chunk at a time.Note ML-014CSV files
G-1641Recall (sensitivity)Of all items that really are positive, the fraction the model found.Note ML-076Precision, recall and F1
G-1642Receptive fieldThe area of the image that one cell (or one unit of a network) responds to.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1643Reciprocal transformReplacing each value with 1/x; reverses the order of the values.Note ML-029Function transformer
G-1644Recommendation engine (recommender system)A model that suggests items, such as movies, that a user is likely to like.Note ML-004Batch (offline) learning
G-1646Recurrent layerA hidden layer whose output at one time step is an input to itself at the next.Note DL-056Recurrent neural network (RNN)
G-1647Recurrent neural network (RNN)A network whose hidden-layer output is fed back in, so it remembers earlier steps of a sequence.Note DL-003Recurrent neural network (RNN)
G-1648RecursionA function that calls itself on smaller inputs.Note DL-019Memoization
G-1649Reduced sample spaceThe outcomes that remain possible once the condition is known.Note MA-015Conditional probability
G-1650Reference categoryThe category whose dummy column is dropped; it is shown by all zeros.Note ML-026One-hot encoding
G-1651ReflectionA transformation that mirrors space, without stretching it (an orthogonal transformation with determinant −1).Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1655RegressionSupervised learning with a numerical output.Note ML-003Regression problems
G-1652Regression metricA number that summarises how close a regression model’s predictions are to the true values.Note ML-051Regression metrics
G-1653Regression output layerThe last layer of a regression network: one node per number to predict, with the linear activation, which returns the weighted sum unchanged so the output can be any number.Note DL-013ANN for regression
G-1654Regression treeA decision tree whose leaves predict numbers: the mean output of their training rows.Note ML-093Regression trees
G-1656Regular expressionA short pattern that describes text, such as \d+ for “one or more digits”.Note ML-032Mixed variables
G-1659RegularisationAdding a penalty for large coefficients to the loss, so the model overfits less (lower variance).Note ML-062Regularisation
G-1657Regularisation by randomisationA name for dropout: reducing overfitting through random choices during training.Note DL-025Dropout
G-1658Regularisation term ΩXGBoost’s penalty on each tree, added to the loss so it prefers small, simple trees: γ for every leaf plus 21​λ times each squared leaf weight, γT+21​λ∑j​wj2​ with T the number of leaves.Note ML-120XGBoost
G-1660Reinforcement learningLearning by acting and receiving rewards or punishments.Note ML-003Reinforcement learning
G-1661Reject H0​The decision that the data gives strong enough evidence against H0​.Note MA-038Hypothesis testing: null and alternative
G-1662Rejection region (critical region)The values of the test statistic for which we reject H0​; its area under H0​ is α.Note MA-039Z-test and rejection regions
G-1663Rejection region approachCarrying out a test by checking whether the test statistic falls beyond a fixed boundary.Note MA-039Z-test and rejection regions
G-1664Relative frequencyA category’s share of all the data: its frequency divided by the total.Note MA-007Frequency tables
G-1665Relative pathA file’s location, starting from the folder the code runs in.Note ML-014CSV files
G-1666Relative positionThe distance between two words, such as “two words later”.Note DL-079Positional encoding
G-1668ReLURectified linear unit, the activation max(0,z): it passes a positive input unchanged and turns a negative one into 0; the usual default activation for hidden layers.Note DL-027ReLU
G-1667ReLU maskThe 0/1 matrix 1[Z>0], with 1 where ReLU’s input was positive and 0 elsewhere; in the backward pass the gradient is multiplied by it, so it flows back only through the positive cells.Note DL-048Backpropagation in a CNN
G-1669remainderThe ColumnTransformer parameter for untouched columns: "drop" (default) or "passthrough".Note ML-027Column transformer
G-2260RepresentationA set of features that describes the data; a good one stays the same when unimportant details (such as handwriting) change.Note DL-002Representation learning
G-1670Representation learning (feature learning)Letting the algorithm discover useful features from raw data, instead of engineering them by hand.Note DL-002Representation learning
G-1671Representation powerThe variety of patterns a network can express; grows with more nodes and layers.Note DL-065Deep (stacked) RNNs
G-1672Representative sampleA sample that reflects the whole situation fairly.Note ML-007Sampling noise and bias
G-1673Request, responseWhat we send to a server, and what it sends back.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-1674requestsPython library that sends web requests.Note ML-016APIs
G-1675Required sample sizeThe smallest sample size that gives a chosen margin of error E, found by solving the margin formula for n: n=(zα/2​σ/E)2.Note MA-036Confidence intervals
G-1676ResamplingChanging the number of rows per class to balance the data.Note ML-127Random under- and oversampling
G-1677Research hypothesisAnother name for the alternative hypothesis: the idea that came out of research.Note MA-038Hypothesis testing: null and alternative
G-1678Reset (modulated) memoryThe GRU’s old memory scaled entry by entry by the reset gate, rt​⊙ht−1​; it sets how much of the past goes into building the candidate hidden state.Note DL-064GRU (gated recurrent unit)
G-1679Reset gate (rt​)A sigmoid layer’s output that decides how much of each entry of the old memory is used to build the candidate.Note DL-064GRU (gated recurrent unit)
G-1680Residual blockA block whose input is added to its output, giving the gradient a shortcut.Note DL-018Skip connections
G-1681Residual connectionA path that skips a sub-layer and adds the sub-layer’s input to its output; also called a skip connection.Note DL-081Residual connections and add & norm
G-1682Residual dropoutDropout applied to each sub-layer’s output before it is added back to the sub-layer’s input (and to the embedding sums); the original transformer uses it to reduce overfitting.Note DL-086Label smoothing
G-2207Residual plotThe residuals (errors) plotted above and below a flat zero line, against a feature or the predicted value; a funnel or a wave in it shows that an assumption of linear regression is broken.Note ML-055Assumptions of linear regression
G-1683Residual streamThe token vector that passes from block to block, to which every sub-layer adds its output.Note DL-087Decoder-only GPT
G-1684Residual sum of squares (sum of squared errors, SSE)The squares of all the errors (residuals) added up; the quantity the best-fit line makes smallest, and a regression tree splits where the SSE of the two sides is smallest.Note ML-051Regression metrics
G-1686ResponseWhat requests.get returns: the status code plus the reply.Note ML-016APIs
G-1687Responsibility rnk​In a mixture model, how likely it is that component k produced point n, given that point (the posterior probability).Note MA-073Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
G-1688RetinaThe 2D sheet of light-sensitive cells at the back of the eye.Note DL-041Convolutional neural network (CNN)
G-1689RetrainTrain a model again, here from scratch on old + new data.Note ML-004Retraining
G-1690Reward / punishmentGood / bad feedback after an action.Note ML-003Reinforcement learning
G-1691Ridge regressionLinear regression with a penalty on the sum of squared coefficients added to the loss; the penalty keeps the coefficients small, which reduces overfitting (L2 regularisation).Note ML-062Ridge regression
G-1692Right singular vector (vi​)A column vi​ of V in the SVD: a unit-length input direction that the matrix sends to σi​ times the matching left singular vector ui​.Note MA-057Singular value decomposition
G-1693Right-tailed and left-tailed testOne-tailed tests that count only one tail as evidence against H0​: a right-tailed test rejects for large values of the test statistic (as for H1​:μ>μ0​), a left-tailed test for small ones (as for H1​:μ<μ0​).Note MA-045Chi-square tests
G-1694RiverA Python library for online machine learning.Note ML-005Online learning
G-1695RLHFReinforcement learning from human feedback: improving a model with a reward model trained on human rankings of its outputs.Note DL-067Large language models (LLMs)
G-1696RMSNormA simpler version of layer normalisation that divides each vector by its root mean square and skips subtracting the mean; many current transformers use it.Note DL-080Layer normalisation
G-1697RMSPropAn optimizer that divides each parameter’s step by the root of a running average (EWMA) of its recent squared gradients, vt​=βvt−1​+(1−β)gt2​; old gradients fade, so unlike AdaGrad the learning rate does not shrink to nothing.Note DL-037RMSProp
G-1698robots.txtA file at a site’s root listing what bots are asked not to visit.Note ML-017Web scraping
G-1699Robust scalingSubtract the median and divide by the interquartile range; copes well with outliers.Note ML-024Feature scaling
